title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to my reporting in his most significant public remarks since the company went public last week:
title_en: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responds to my reporting in his most significant public remarks since the company went public last week:
title_zh: Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 在他自上周公司上市以来最重要的公开讲话中回应了我的报道：
author: @MadisonMills22
summary_zh: Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 向所有希望将治理外包给聊天机器人的人传达了一条信息。他说，将治理交给人工智能是一个坏主意。阿莫代的核心观点很简单。
article_content:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has a message for anyone hoping to outsource governance to a chatbot. Handing governance over to AI, he says, is a bad idea.

Amodei’s core point is simple. Advanced AI systems should not take over the job of governing humans.

His comments have also stirred disagreement across the industry. A November 25, 2026 Axios article outlined friction between competing views among AI leaders.

That report noted rival AI executives publicly critiquing Amodei’s positions on AI decision-making in critical situations. It also pointed back to his earlier remarks suggesting AI could effectively manage critical tasks in a future economy.

So the picture is more layered than a simple pro-human versus pro-machine split. Amodei appears comfortable with AI doing serious work in the economy. Where he draws the line is letting it hold the keys to governance itself.

Amodei’s warning arrives shortly after a major financial milestone for Anthropic. The company went public on Nasdaq on November 19, 2026, in what the research describes as the largest IPO in history.

During his IPO speech, he emphasized that Anthropic would pace its AI training and deployment to make sure safety stays a priority.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Anthropic has also built a structural guardrail into the company. It established a Long-Term Benefit Trust, designed to keep the company’s mission ahead of investor pressure.

The governance comment is not a one-off. In September 2026, Amodei published an essay calling for a slowdown in frontier AI development.

His stated concern in that essay was recursive self-improvement. That is the scenario where AI systems become capable of improving their own design, which then makes them better at improving themselves again.

For the AI industry, Amodei’s stance sharpens a debate that has been simmering for years. The question is no longer just whether AI can do a given task. It is who gets to decide, and who answers when something goes wrong.

The Axios report suggests that rival executives do not all see this the same way. That split matters because the companies building frontier AI also shape how it gets deployed in courts, agencies, financial systems, and critical infrastructure.

The research frames the current moment as one that signals growing regulatory oversight and scrutiny across the AI sector.

For investors, the picture is more nuanced than a typical tech listing. Anthropic is now a public company that has openly told shareholders it plans to move deliberately rather than at maximum speed. The Long-Term Benefit Trust also means shareholders have limited ability to push the company off its mission.

Disclosure: This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. For more information on how we create and review content, see our Editorial Policy.

title: One week after Anthropic's IPO, the internal debate at the company is whether they should keep releasing models to the public or keep everything for internal use and leave humanity's decisions in the hands of a superintelligent AI.
title_en: One week after Anthropic's IPO, the internal debate at the company is whether they should keep releasing models to the public or keep everything for internal use and leave humanity's decisions in the hands of a superintelligent AI.
title_zh: Anthropic 首次公开募股一周后，公司内部争论的是他们是否应该继续向公众发布模型，还是保留所有内容供内部使用，并将人类的决定权交给超级智能人工智能。
author: @TokenGremlin

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic 首次公开募股一周后，公司内部争论的是他们是否应该继续向公众发布模型，还是保留所有内容供内部使用，并将人类的决定权交给超级智能人工智能。 巨额融资意向凸显出头部模型公司在研发前沿架构与构建超级计算集群过程中巨大的资本消耗率，企业正力求在公开上市前锁定充沛流动性以构筑壁垒。

article_content:
HONG KONG, Aug. 13, 2026 (SEND2PRESS NEWSWIRE) — AI Inspo announced the availability of Seedance 2.5 on its creative platform on Aug. 7, giving users access to the latest AI video technology through a simple, cost-effective workspace. The platform brings multiple generative AI models together in one place, allowing users to explore and create without switching between different services.

Image caption: Seedance 2.5 is now available on AI Inspo for 30-second AI video generation.

Seedance 2.5 is available now on AI Inspo: https://www.ai-inspo.com/model/seedance-2-5

Seedance 2.5 is designed to maintain character and scene consistency across longer shots while delivering realistic motion and smooth transitions. Compared with the previous 15-second limit, Seedance 2.5 extends maximum duration to 30 seconds and adds native audio, helping creators produce more complete visual stories within a single workflow.

Seedance 2.5 is well suited for social media content, product commercials, cinematic sequences, and other short-form video projects, combining longer video durations, multimodal references, and native audio in a single workflow.

Seedance 2.5 supports multimodal inputs, allowing users to combine text, image, video, and audio references in a single workflow. On AI Inspo, it enables both text-to-video and image-to-video generation with native audio. Users can also adjust video duration, aspect ratio, camera movement, and output resolution to fit their creative needs.

From social media posts and product commercials to cinematic sequences and visual storytelling, Seedance 2.5 suits a wide range of short-form video projects.

Through AI Inspo’s browser-based workspace, users can upload reference materials, enter prompts, generate videos, preview results, refine their ideas, and export finished content without installing additional software. New users can also claim free credits to try Seedance 2.5.

AI Inspo is a browser-based creative workspace that brings AI video, image, and music generation together in one platform. It gives creators access to leading generative AI models, including Seedance 2.5, Veo 3, Kling 3.0, and MiniMax H3, through a single interface.

Built for creators, marketers, and businesses, AI Inspo makes AI-powered content creation more accessible and efficient. By bringing the latest AI models and creative technologies into one cost-effective workspace, the platform enables users to explore different tools and create content without switching between multiple services.

More information: https://www.ai-inspo.com/

VIDEO (YouTube): https://youtu.be/yYBRDjQXGVE

IMAGE link: https://www.Send2Press.com/300dpi/26-0813-s2p-aiinspo-300dpi.webp

Video may contain AI generated “people.”

article_content:
ByteDance raised the ceiling on AI video generation Tuesday when it announced Seedance 2.5 at the Volcano Engine FORCE conference in Beijing — a model that, the company claims, can generate a single continuous 30-second clip without stitching shorter segments together. If those claims survive independent testing when the model launches in early July, Seedance 2.5 will mark the first major closed commercial AI video tool to reach that duration natively, without segment breaks.

The announcement arrives four months after ByteDance voluntarily paused the global rollout of its predecessor, Seedance 2.0, following cease-and-desist letters from every major Hollywood studio over alleged copyright infringement. Those legal disputes remain unresolved. The central question hanging over the June 23 event is whether Seedance 2.5 carries the same legal exposure — or whether the intervening months of remediation work have changed the equation for enterprise buyers.

Until now, professional AI video generators from Runway Gen-4.5, Google Veo 3.1, and OpenAI's Sora 2 — which was shut down on April 26, 2026 — topped out at roughly 8 to 15 seconds per native clip. Generating longer sequences required stitching shorter clips end-to-end, a process that introduces visible seams between segments, character faces that drift in appearance between shots, and lighting inconsistencies that mark the footage as artificial. Television commercials, social media ads, explainer videos, and short documentary segments all cluster in the 15–60 second range. A tool that can hold visual and audio consistency across an entire half-minute without a stitch changes the production economics for that entire format category.

ByteDance describes the architecture behind that consistency as a unified joint audio-video generation system, in which visual and audio signals are co-processed inside the same latent space rather than generated separately and synchronized after the fact. Combined with what the company calls optimized spatial-temporal attention mechanisms, the model holds character appearance, lighting, and motion style across the full clip duration. ByteDance announced Seedance 2.5 on stage, not as a shipped product — it is currently in global enterprise beta, with a public launch targeted for early July 2026. No pricing has been disclosed. All claimed capabilities are ByteDance's own statements; no independent benchmarks exist yet for Seedance 2.5.

Seedance 2.5 ships with three generation modes. Text-to-video produces a clip from a written prompt alone. Image-to-video animates a still image into a moving scene. A motion-reference mode uses an existing video clip to guide the movement style of a new generation — useful for advertisers or filmmakers who want to replicate a specific camera technique or action choreography without sourcing live footage.

The model's reference input capacity is a more significant upgrade than the generation modes alone suggest. Seedance 2.5 accepts up to 50 simultaneous multimodal reference materials — images, video clips, and audio files — compared to roughly 12 in Seedance 2.0. Volcano Engine president Tan Dai told the conference that this capacity is designed for brand-consistency and episodic storytelling workflows, where the model must lock a character's face, a product's appearance, an art style, and a music reference across an entire generation without drifting. Google's Veo 3.1, the closest Western competitor for reference control, accepts only three reference inputs — making the gap between the two substantial for production use cases that require strict consistency.

The system also introduces localized region editing: a creator can redraw one specific element in a frame — swap a character's clothing, change a background element, alter a product in a scene — without regenerating the entire clip. That capability addresses one of the most costly friction points in AI video production, where fixing one small error currently requires starting over and hoping the rest of the output survives intact.

How the Architecture Differs From Seedance 2.0

The distinction between Seedance 2.0 and 2.5 is not simply longer output — it is a change in how longer output is produced. Seedance 2.0 could produce clips of up to 15 seconds natively, and could reach 30 seconds only through sequential stitching, which meant extended output was a composite of shorter generated segments joined at their boundaries. Seedance 2.5, according to ByteDance, generates the entire 30-second clip as a single coherent diffusion pass. The spatial-temporal attention mechanisms that enable this hold object identity and scene state across a longer temporal horizon than previous diffusion window approaches could sustain.

ByteDance's predecessor had already established an independent quality benchmark before this announcement. On the Artificial Analysis Video Arena — a blind human-preference leaderboard that assigns scores through paired comparisons — Seedance 2.0 currently ranks first for text-to-video with audio, with an Elo score of 1,218, ahead of Kling 3.0 and Google Veo 3.1. That ranking reflects the shipping version of Seedance 2.0. No Seedance 2.5 score exists yet; benchmark numbers will not be reliable until the model is publicly available and independently tested.

ByteDance also announced at the same event that Seedance 2.0 has been upgraded to support native 4K output with 10-bit color depth — a separate improvement that benefits development teams already integrated with the current model. The company said its enterprise Seedance platform has reached $2 billion in annual recurring revenue, a figure that signals commercial traction ahead of the 2.5 launch.

Seedance 2.5 will be distributed through ByteDance's Volcano Engine cloud platform, with additional reach through CapCut — the video editing application with more than 400 million monthly active users — as well as the Dreamina and Doubao consumer interfaces.

Before committing to a Seedance 2.5 integration, development teams should weigh several operational factors that the conference announcement left unresolved.

No independent benchmark exists yet. All described capabilities — 30-second single-pass generation, 50-reference input handling, regional editing stability — are ByteDance's stated specifications from the June 23 keynote. They are consistent across multiple reporters covering the event and are plausible given the architecture, but they have not been verified by third-party testing. Early July access will provide the first real opportunity for external evaluation.

Copyright filters are active. Following the Motion Picture Association's formal cease-and-desist action against Seedance 2.0 in February 2026, ByteDance added content filters that block generation of recognizable real faces and copyrighted characters. Those filters remain active in the current model and are expected to carry forward into 2.5.

Pricing is undisclosed. Seedance 2.0 was priced at roughly $2.50 per 15-second clip on some third-party inference platforms. Seedance 2.5's cost structure has not been announced and may change the cost-per-second economics of longer clips.

The Unresolved Copyright Situation From Seedance 2.0

The context a developer evaluating Seedance 2.5 cannot ignore is the legal record of its predecessor. When Seedance 2.0 launched in China in February 2026, the Motion Picture Association described the tool's copyright infringement as "a feature, not a bug" in a formal cease-and-desist letter — the first such letter the MPA had ever sent to a major generative AI company. Disney, Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount, Netflix, Sony Pictures, and Universal all sent their own cease-and-desist letters within days of the launch. SAG-AFTRA condemned the model's ability to produce realistic actor likenesses without consent.

ByteDance pledged to strengthen safeguards and voluntarily paused the global rollout in March 2026. As of May 2026, no federal lawsuit had been filed in the United States and no government had formally banned the model in any country — though US Senators Marsha Blackburn and Peter Welch had written to ByteDance's CEO demanding the model be shut down. The enforcement challenge is partly structural: serving legal process on a China-based company under the Hague Convention takes an estimated 18 to 24 months, a timeline that has given Chinese AI video companies a significant advantage over Hollywood's legal timeline.

ByteDance previewed a new AI copyright commercialization platform at the same FORCE conference, with filmmaker Stephen Chow named as an initial partner. Whether that platform meaningfully addresses the concerns raised by the studios — or whether the same generation capabilities that triggered Seedance 2.0's controversy carry forward into Seedance 2.5 — will only be assessed once independent testers gain public access in July.

ByteDance is headquartered in Beijing. China's National Intelligence Law, passed in June 2017, requires under Article 7 that "all organizations and citizens shall support, assist, and cooperate with national intelligence efforts in accordance with law." That requirement applies to ByteDance and its subsidiaries. China's Cybersecurity Law (2017) additionally requires businesses operating in China to store data on servers within China and permits Chinese authorities to conduct spot inspections of network operations.

The Chinese government holds a 1% "golden share" with a board seat in ByteDance's main Chinese subsidiary, Beijing ByteDance Technology, with a government official whose background is in propaganda appointed to that seat. ByteDance has maintained an internal Chinese Communist Party committee since 2014. The company has a strategic partnership with China's Ministry of Public Security. The US Department of Homeland Security has assessed that Chinese companies are "required to secretly share data with the PRC government or other entities upon request, even if that request is illegal under the jurisdiction in which these firms operate."

ByteDance has denied sharing user data with the Chinese government and states that its data practices comply with US law. Legal scholars have noted that the scope of Article 7's compulsion is contested: an analysis by China Law Translate argues the law may not require active participation in intelligence gathering beyond standard law enforcement cooperation requirements. Neither ByteDance's denial nor the scholarly debate changes the structural legal condition: a Chinese government request to ByteDance for enterprise API usage data, inference logs, or developer-submitted content would be made under a legal framework that does not require disclosure to the affected party.

Enterprise teams integrating Seedance 2.5 into their production pipelines should assess what data they plan to submit to the model — including reference content, brand assets, scripts, and proprietary visual material — against this legal condition before committing to the integration.

What the Seedance 2.5 Launch Does and Does Not Change

For the AI video production market, the 30-second native generation milestone matters even with a qualification attached. The realistic ceiling among major commercial models before this announcement was 8 to 15 seconds per native clip. Seedance 2.5's stated capability, if confirmed by independent testing, at minimum doubles that ceiling among closed commercial tools and removes the stitching step that has been the primary technical barrier to professional-grade long-form AI video.

The model that arrives in July will enter a market where its predecessor already holds the top rank on the leading independent benchmark, where the copyright compliance architecture is still being tested, and where the geopolitical context of its maker's home jurisdiction is a material enterprise decision — not a footnote. Developers who evaluate Seedance 2.5 on technical capability alone will have an incomplete picture. Those who factor in the copyright framework, the data jurisdiction conditions, and the still-pending independent verification of the 30-second claim will be better positioned to make the integration decision that matches their actual risk tolerance.

When can developers actually use Seedance 2.5?

As of the June 23, 2026 announcement, Seedance 2.5 is in global enterprise beta with limited access for qualifying organizations. ByteDance's stated target for public launch is early July 2026. A precise date has not been confirmed. Third-party platforms that have integrated Seedance 2.0 have indicated they will add 2.5 access once the official Volcano Engine API opens. Pricing has not been disclosed.

Does Seedance 2.5 resolve the copyright problems that shut down Seedance 2.0's global launch?

ByteDance has not made specific claims that Seedance 2.5's safeguards address all of the concerns raised by the Motion Picture Association and the major Hollywood studios in February and March 2026. The legal disputes from Seedance 2.0 — including the MPA's formal cease-and-desist characterizing infringement as "a feature, not a bug" — have not been resolved in court. ByteDance did announce a new AI copyright commercialization platform at the same event, but the relationship between that platform's licensing mechanisms and Seedance 2.5's generation safeguards has not been publicly documented. Independent testers who gain early July access will be in the first position to evaluate whether the generation capabilities that produced unauthorized character likenesses in Seedance 2.0 persist in 2.5.

What is technically different about native 30-second generation versus stitched-together clips?

Stitched generation assembles shorter clips — typically 5 to 15 seconds — end-to-end in post-processing. The boundaries between segments produce visible shifts in character appearance, lighting, and motion style, because each segment was generated independently with only limited conditioning from the previous one. Seedance 2.5's claimed approach processes the entire 30-second output as a single coherent diffusion pass, using spatial-temporal attention mechanisms to maintain scene state — character identity, lighting conditions, camera position — from the first frame to the last without segment breaks. Whether that claim holds under independent testing with complex prompts, multiple characters, and varied motion is unknown until public access opens.

Should enterprise teams using Seedance 2.5 be concerned about where their content goes?

ByteDance is headquartered in China and subject to China's National Intelligence Law (2017), which requires organizations to cooperate with national intelligence requests. Enterprise teams that submit proprietary brand assets, scripts, reference videos, or other confidential materials through the Seedance API are submitting that content to infrastructure operated by a company under that legal jurisdiction. ByteDance has stated it does not share user data with the Chinese government and maintains data practices compliant with US law. The structural legal condition — that a government request under Chinese law would not require notification to the data owner — does not change based on that denial. Enterprise security teams should evaluate this as a data governance question before integrating Seedance 2.5 into workflows that handle sensitive client or proprietary material.

ai_analysis.insight_en: This move indicates Google's attempt to tighten control over the AI agent ecosystem by centralizing access protocols to mitigate fragmented security and compliance risks. ai_analysis.takeaway_en: If validated, this algorithmic breakthrough could pose a significant threat to existing asymmetric encryption standards, necessitating rigorous peer review. This signals that AI models are transitioning from generative tasks to independent scientific discovery, likely accelerating the innovation cycle in computational mathematics.

title: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks https://t.co/6LyVQo7wiH
title_en: As MCP turns two, Claude gets Skills over MCP and better support for long-running tasks https://t.co/6LyVQo7wiH
title_zh: 随着 MCP 两岁生日，Claude 获得了超过 MCP 的技能，并为长时间运行的任务提供了更好的支持
author: @thenewstack
summary_en: Marking the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Anthropic has launched the public beta of 'Skills over MCP.' This enables servers to provide structured workflows rather than just tool definitions, while also launching general availability for 'Tasks' and 'Elicitation' to handle long-running, interactive agentic workflows.
summary_zh: Anthropic发布Model Context Protocol（MCP）周年更新，推出Skills公测版及Tasks与Elicitation功能，强化AI与复杂服务器任务的交互协作能力。
article_content:
Anthropic enhances Claude with Skills over MCP in public beta, Tasks, Elicitation, and upcoming File Uploads for improved AI-server collaboration.

Anthropic has announced significant updates to its AI platform Claude, marking the second anniversary of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). These updates include the public beta release of Skills over MCP, the general availability of Tasks and Elicitation, and the upcoming rollout of File Uploads. These features aim to enhance Claude's ability to collaborate with MCP servers for more complex and interactive tasks.

Skills over MCP is now in public beta, enabling MCP servers to publish skills alongside their tools. Unlike tool names and descriptions, which only indicate functionality, Skills provide step-by-step workflows, best practices, and tailored playbooks for specific use cases. This allows Claude to handle longer, multi-step tasks efficiently by loading skills only when needed, reducing context usage. Skills automatically update with server changes, requiring no separate installations for users.

Examples of Skills over MCP in action include Shopify assisting with end-to-end online store design, HubSpot onboarding customers, Atlassian leveraging organizational insights, and Carta drafting equity documents from uploaded files. Skills over MCP is available by default for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and can be enabled for Team plans by administrators. Enterprise availability is expected soon.

Tasks and Elicitation are now generally available, addressing the need for servers to manage long-running, interactive work. Tasks allow servers to execute time-intensive operations or full agent loops in the background while Claude continues other tasks. For instance, ZoomInfo uses Tasks for in-depth account and contact research that previously required multiple prompts.

Elicitation enables servers to pause operations to seek user input for critical decisions, such as spending approvals or data deletions. Examples include Supabase confirming costs before creating paid projects, Railway seeking confirmation before removing services, and GitHub requiring repository names before deletions. These features are available for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans and are rolling out to Team and Enterprise plans.

The upcoming File Uploads feature will allow Claude to send and receive files, such as PDFs, spreadsheets, and images, directly to MCP servers without relying on the context window. This extension is expected to streamline workflows by enabling seamless file-based interactions. File Uploads will be available for Pro, Max, Ultra, and eligible Team and Enterprise plans.

Since its launch two years ago, MCP has become a foundational standard for connecting AI agents to data systems, with over 700 million monthly SDK downloads and more than 10,000 MCP connectors for Claude. Recent improvements include enhanced token efficiency, scalability, simplified authorization through Enterprise Managed Auth, and interactive interfaces via MCP Apps. These developments aim to make MCP more accessible and reliable for developers and organizations.

Anthropic's latest updates underscore its commitment to advancing AI-server collaboration, providing tools that enable agents like Claude to perform more autonomously and effectively in production environments.

full_text_en: I built an autonomous system of 16 agents with Claude Code. The first two weeks went to process, not product. Here's what broke and what I changed. #aiagents #claudecode...Show more
summary_zh: 开发者利用Claude Code构建由16个代理组成的自治系统，探索从底层流程构建向最终产品交付的演进。
summary_en: A developer built an autonomous system comprising 16 agents using Claude Code. The project initially focused on workflow orchestration and debugging complex agentic interactions, transitioning from systemic process building to final product delivery.
article_content_zh:
在构建多代理系统的过程中，研发者发现核心难点在于处理系统性损坏（Systemic Failure）。通过Claude Code，研发者将初期重心放在代理协作流程（Workflow）的编排上，而非急于产出功能模块。

项目调整重点在于优化多代理状态机的上下文传递逻辑，确保系统在面临复杂代码变更时能自动处理依赖冲突，从而实现了从纯粹研发流程到实际工程产品的跨越。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 开发者基于Anthropic推出的Claude Code工具构建了包含16个协作节点的自治代理系统。该项目在初期侧重于研发工作流的逻辑编排与故障调试，旨在解决多代理环境下的任务分配与状态一致性问题，目前已推进至产品化交付阶段。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: A developer built an autonomous system comprising 16 agents using Claude Code. The project initially focused on workflow orchestration and debugging complex agentic interactions, transitioning from systemic process building to final product delivery.

elements_zh.what: 部署16个代理组成的自治系统，重构流程逻辑以适配产品交付需求
elements_zh.why: 旨在验证多代理协作在复杂工程任务中的鲁棒性与自动化效率

elements_en.what: Deployed an autonomous system of 16 agents, refactoring workflows for product delivery
elements_en.why: To validate the robustness and efficiency of multi-agent collaboration in complex engineering tasks

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 多代理系统（MAS）的研发重心正从单点任务自动化向长链条、高可靠性的产品级工作流迁移。Claude Code类工具显著降低了环境配置门槛，但多代理间的上下文传递与冲突裁决仍是当前系统架构设计的关键技术瓶颈。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The focus of Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) is shifting from discrete task automation to high-reliability, long-chain product workflows. While tools like Claude Code significantly lower the barrier to entry, resolving context propagation and conflict arbitration remains the primary technical bottleneck for production-grade agentic architecture.

author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI research team published a mathematical proof establishing that the exponent for matrix multiplication is exactly 2.25. This result challenges long-standing theoretical assumptions regarding the lower bound of computational complexity.

ai_analysis.digest_zh: 针对AI Agent交互范式，技术专家质疑为何Agent应沿用人类导向的UI设计，而非通过API或模型上下文协议（MCP）直接访问后端逻辑。这种观点强调，UI不仅存在渲染开销，且其复杂交互逻辑对自动化程序而言是冗余的负担。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Tech experts are challenging the paradigm of AI Agents interacting with human-centric UIs, arguing for direct backend access via APIs or the Model Context Protocol (MCP). This shift aims to eliminate the inherent inefficiency and overhead of parsing visual interfaces during automated task execution.
key_points_zh: 核心诉求：弃用基于UI的Agent交互，转而推行直接的API/MCP调用
技术痛点：人机界面存在冗余的渲染开销与交互逻辑障碍
行业趋势：AI自动化执行效率将由系统的API开放度直接决定
key_points_en: Core argument: Moving away from UI-based agent interaction toward direct API/MCP invocation
Technical pain point: Inefficiency and overhead inherent in UI-based parsing
Industry trend: AI execution efficiency will be defined by the openness of system-level APIs
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: AI Agent的交互形态正在发生从‘模拟人操作’向‘语义化指令调用’的范式转换。长期看，标准化的API与MCP基础设施将取代传统的UI自动化，促使后端API的语义开放程度成为衡量SaaS产品AI原生能力的核心指标。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: The interaction paradigm for AI agents is shifting from 'human-like simulation' to 'semantic instruction invocation.' Standardized API and MCP infrastructure will eventually replace traditional UI automation, making the semantic openness of backend APIs a key metric for AI-native product competitiveness.

title: Wide beams, lower tail latency. At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators. H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDI
title_en: Wide beams, lower tail latency. At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators. H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDI
title_zh: vLLM-GR大幅降低大模型尾部延迟
author: vLLM Project
author_role: 高通量、低内存显存极速推理架构
summary_en: The vLLM project team introduced the vLLM-GR backend, optimized for wide beam search scenarios. Tested on H20 accelerators with a batch size of 8, it achieved a P99 tail latency of 369.4ms, significantly outperforming SGLang's 1280.1ms.
summary_zh: vLLM-GR后端在多加速器环境下表现出优于SGLang的P99延迟，特别在H20等型号上性能提升显著。
full_text_zh: 宽波束，尾部延迟更低。在波束宽度为 256 和 1,024 个输入令牌时，vLLM-GR 在所有六个加速器上以批量大小 4 和 8 显示的后端中记录了最低的 P99。 H20，批次 8：369.4 毫秒对比 SGLang 的 1,280.1 毫秒和 NVIDI 的 428.1 毫秒
quote_zh: 宽波束，尾部延迟更低。在波束宽度为 256 和 1,024 个输入令牌时，vLLM-GR 在所有六个加速器上以批量大小 4 和 8 显示的后端中记录了最低的 P99。 H20，第 8 批：369.4 m
full_text_en: Wide beams, lower tail latency. At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators. H20, batch 8: 369.4 ms vs. 1,280.1 ms for SGLang and 428.1 ms for NVIDI
quote_en: Wide beams, lower tail latency. At beam width 256 and 1,024 input tokens, vLLM-GR recorded the lowest P99 among the backends shown at batch sizes 4 and 8 on all six accelerators. H20, batch 8: 369.4 m

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: vLLM项目团队推出vLLM-GR后端，针对宽束搜索（Wide Beams）场景进行了专项优化。在H20加速器、batch size为8的测试环境下，其P99尾部延迟降至369.4ms，显著优于SGLang的1280.1ms。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: The vLLM project team introduced the vLLM-GR backend, optimized for wide beam search scenarios. Tested on H20 accelerators with a batch size of 8, it achieved a P99 tail latency of 369.4ms, significantly outperforming SGLang's 1280.1ms.

elements_zh.where: AI推理部署后端基准测试

elements_zh.why: 解决大规模参数模型在复杂搜索场景下的高延迟痛点

elements_en.what: Released vLLM-GR backend with H20 latency benchmarks
elements_en.why: Addressing high tail latency in large-scale model wide beam search

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 在大参数模型推理中，算子调度效率已成为影响服务SLA的关键瓶颈，尤其是针对受限算力（如H20）的优化直接决定了企业侧私有化部署的成本结构。vLLM通过调整计算后端逻辑实现差异化性能提升，加剧了推理框架市场的技术选型竞争。
ai_analysis.insight_en: In large-model inference, kernel scheduling efficiency is now a critical SLA bottleneck, particularly for constrained hardware like H20, which dictates the unit cost of enterprise deployment. vLLM’s performance gains via backend optimization intensify technical competition in the inference framework market.

title: ChatGPT Ads are opening up the playing field for smaller brands to compete:
title_en: ChatGPT Ads are opening up the playing field for smaller brands to compete:
title_zh: OpenAI构建AI代理驱动的广告投放系统
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI is scaling an ad system driven by an AI agent called the 'orchestrator,' which interprets user prompts and historical context to generate relevant queries for ad auctions. Unlike traditional keyword-based systems, this approach targets the user's 'consideration phase' to match intent with commercial outcomes.
summary_zh: OpenAI正测试由AI代理“Orchestrator”主导的广告系统，通过分析对话语境与历史偏好，实现更精准的意图匹配与广告拍卖。
article_content:
Buyers have been clamoring to understand more about ChatGPT's ads system since it launched in February. Executives have been slowly revealing more.

OpenAI matches ChatGPT ads to search queries written by its own AI agent, three executives who run the AI lab's ad system told ADWEEK.

When a user writes a prompt in ChatGPT, an AI agent OpenAI calls the orchestrator reads the conversation and works out what the person might want to buy. It can also draw on the user's previous chats when the user’s ad personalization settings allow it. It then writes its own search queries, ranks the ads it finds in its system, and sends the best candidates to an auction that weighs advertisers' bids against how useful each ad is likely to be to the user.

“It's like a completely made-up query that is not in the user's search at all," OpenAI engineer Ritendra Datta told ADWEEK.

For instance, the agent could query: “Find me boots that are great for someone who also loves skiing,” for someone who is currently asking about boots but has talked about skiing in past ChatGPT conversations.

The agent can also search categories the user hasn't raised. For someone planning a winter trip to Yosemite, it might pull ads for snow gear and then hotels near the park, and weigh both in the auction. Datta declined to say how far back into a person's chat history the agent searches.

Advertisers can enter targeting parameters such as keywords and location, said OpenAI’s CTO of applications, Vijaye Raji, and the system combines them with what it knows about a user for what he called "intent matching."

"ChatGPT sits in a unique place, which is the consideration phase,” Raji said. "It's a multifaceted, multi-dimensional conversation, which is where we think we're extremely good at matching that intent," he added. By comparison, he called searches on Google and Facebook "one-dimensional."

ChatGPT's ad system requires advertisers to trust the platform to place their ad in the most appropriate conversation. OpenAI’s head of monetization, Benji Shomair, recently said that user trust guides its ads business.

"In Search, we choose the query, and in Social and standard programmatic, we choose the audience," said Ben Kahan, head of programmatic, North America, Brainlabs. "On ChatGPT, a model decides the conversation, and our keywords act as hints rather than hard targeting. It’s a step down in control."

An OpenAI spokesperson said its system uses "multiple signals," including "the ad’s landing page, title, copy, advertiser-provided context hints and targeting selections, and, when ads personalization is enabled, select signals from a user’s broader ChatGPT experience. OpenAI declined to share how many people have opted into ads personalization.

Asked whether advertisers could expect prompt- or intent-level reports in the future, Raji said no. Instead, advertisers get aggregated reports that say, "We showed ads for these many users and here are the conversions," he said.

Two media agency executives interviewed for this story said OpenAI's ad practices are not entirely transparent.

"Transparency is very weak; no visibility into the matching logic or why an ad matched or what the prompt was," said Kahan. "There's also no delivery guarantees. If matching logic is also using chat history, advertisers will want a clearer account of what their dollars are doing, both for performance and brand safety."

The OpenAI spokesperson said the company does "not currently offer delivery guarantees," but advertisers can get insights like "impressions, clicks, spend and attributed conversions."

Several advertisers ADWEEK has spoken with in recent months still treat ChatGPT ads as a test because they can't tie its ads to business outcomes. One retail client saw a 0.91% click-through rate on its ChatGPT ads, well below the roughly 6.4% benchmark for Google Search campaigns in the same sector, ADWEEK previously reported.

"On Google, for almost every search about a product or service in the developed world, Google has at least one relevant advertiser," said Phillip Thune, CEO of Adthena. "ChatGPT, despite having over 100,000 advertisers, is nowhere close, especially for local prompts like best house painter near me."

Google, it's worth remembering, has several decades' worth of experience in selling ads.

OpenAI is investing in “a lot of measurement capabilities,” Raji said, including conversion API and pixels, to help buyers track what happens on their platform after someone clicks on a ChatGPT ad.

“The goal would be to show the value of acquisition,” he said.

OpenAI has signed Criteo, Amazon, PubMatic and Magnite, among others, to bring more advertisers into ChatGPT. The three executives said the company has no current plans for an ad network or to open ChatGPT inventory to real-time bidding, though neither ruled them out.

OpenAI said it hit $1 billion in annualized run rate in August—a figure that counts advertiser spend across every market where ChatGPT ads run. Raji said, "The $1 billion back then was a much smaller footprint than what we have now.” He declined to share new figures. OpenAI is aiming to reach $2.5 billion in ad revenue this year.

OpenAI also made inroads into generative engine optimization (GEO) with Business Hub, a tool that helps brands manage how people interact with their business and see how they show up in ChatGPT conversations.

"I don't think that's going to stop third-party tools," said Job Roberts, chief innovation officer, People Inc., during an IAB roundtable earlier this month, referring to the litany of GEO vendors that have sprung up in the last few years. "Because grading your own homework has always had limited benefit."

Update: This article has been updated to clarify that ChatGPT can only draw on past chats when the user’s ad personalization settings allow it.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI正在推进由AI代理（Orchestrator）主导的广告系统，该代理能实时分析用户提问及历史对话语境，生成匹配的搜索查询并参与竞价。与传统基于关键词的搜索广告不同，该系统致力于在用户购买决策的“考虑期”介入，通过意图匹配提供更具相关性的商业建议。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI is scaling an ad system driven by an AI agent called the 'orchestrator,' which interprets user prompts and historical context to generate relevant queries for ad auctions. Unlike traditional keyword-based systems, this approach targets the user's 'consideration phase' to match intent with commercial outcomes.

elements_zh.who: Ritendra Datta（OpenAI工程师），Vijaye Raji（OpenAI应用首席技术官），Benji Shomair（OpenAI货币化主管）
elements_zh.where: ChatGPT平台广告系统测试
elements_zh.what: 通过AI代理实时捕捉对话语境并生成搜索意图，进行个性化广告匹配与拍卖
elements_zh.why: 利用ChatGPT在决策考虑期的天然优势，将意图转化为高价值商业流量

elements_en.who: Ritendra Datta (Engineer), Vijaye Raji (CTO of Apps), Benji Shomair (Head of Monetization)
elements_en.what: AI agent orchestrator extracts conversation intent to trigger dynamic ad auctions
elements_en.why: Leveraging ChatGPT’s unique positioning in the purchase consideration phase to monetize user intent

ai_analysis.insight_zh: OpenAI的广告策略标志着从“关键词匹配”向“意图推理”的范式转移，这直接挑战了谷歌搜索广告基于精确查询的垄断性地位。随着AI代理在决策链路中权重增加，广告主的获客逻辑将从优化关键词转向优化“对话话术”，这将显著改变数字营销的颗粒度与透明度博弈。
ai_analysis.insight_en: OpenAI’s ad strategy signals a paradigm shift from keyword matching to intent inference, directly challenging Google’s dominance in search-driven advertising. As AI agents gain influence in decision-making paths, advertisers must pivot from keyword bidding to optimizing conversational context, redefining the rules of digital marketing.

系统结合用户历史数据与多维度意图匹配，提升广告精准度
改变了广告主仅依靠关键词投放的模式，转向需适应模型决策逻辑的“意图引导”
key_points_en: The 'Orchestrator' AI agent interprets conversational context to generate dynamic ad auction queries.
System leverages user history and intent matching to enhance ad relevance beyond single-dimensional searches.
Advertisers are forced to adapt from static keyword bidding to dynamic, model-driven conversational placement.

As AI agents gain influence in decision-making paths, advertisers must pivot from keyword bidding to optimizing conversational context, redefining the rules of digital marketing.

title_zh: 谷歌设定第三方AI代理接入其办公组件的最终期限
full_text_zh: 2027 年 2 月 1 日：这是 Google 为任何涉及 Gmail、云端硬盘、日历、聊天或任务的第三方 AI 代理设定的硬性截止日期。该日期之后没有侧门，只有 MCP。该政策于今天正式发布，同时所有八个 Workspace MCP 均全面可用
full_text_en: February 1, 2027: that's the hard deadline Google just set for any third-party AI agent touching Gmail, Drive, Calendar, Chat or Tasks. No side doors after that date, only MCP. The policy landed today alongside general availability for all eight Workspace MCP s
summary_zh: 谷歌明确2027年2月1日起，所有连接Gmail、云端硬盘等Workspace组件的第三方AI代理必须完全遵循MCP协议。
summary_en: Google has established a hard deadline of February 1, 2027, for all third-party AI agents interacting with Workspace components like Gmail, Drive, and Calendar. After this date, all access must be mediated through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), effectively deprecating non-standard legacy interfaces, alongside the immediate availability of eight Workspace MCP modules.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌已发布硬性政策，设定2027年2月1日为涉及Gmail、云端硬盘、日历及任务等Workspace组件的第三方AI代理准入截止日期。届时，所有第三方接入必须完全通过机器上下文协议（MCP）实现，彻底封闭任何非标准化接口，并同步宣布八个Workspace MCP模块全面上线。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google has established a hard deadline of February 1, 2027, for all third-party AI agents interacting with Workspace components like Gmail, Drive, and Calendar. After this date, all access must be mediated through the Model Context Protocol (MCP), effectively deprecating non-standard legacy interfaces, alongside the immediate availability of eight Workspace MCP modules.

elements_zh.where: Google Workspace生态环境
elements_zh.what: 强制推行MCP协议作为第三方AI代理接入的唯一标准，取消非标准接口
elements_zh.why: 通过MCP实现更安全的语义交互，强化谷歌对生态数据流动与权限管控的闭环

elements_en.what: Mandating Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the sole standard for third-party AI agents, deprecating legacy APIs
elements_en.why: To standardize secure semantic interactions and tighten control over data flows and permissions within the ecosystem

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 谷歌强制推进MCP协议旨在通过技术手段垄断AI代理与私有数据交互的标准定义权。通过将第三方代理强制纳入统一的协议栈，谷歌不仅降低了数据治理风险，还实质上确立了其Workspace作为‘AI代理操作系统’的核心平台地位，使外部开发者的功能增量必须完全依赖其生态架构。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Google's enforcement of MCP aims to monopolize the standard definitions for AI agents interacting with proprietary data. By funneling third-party agents into a unified protocol stack, Google mitigates data governance risks and cements its Workspace as the foundational 'OS for AI agents,' forcing external developers into total ecosystem dependency.

title: OpenAI published the pretraining loss of all of its frontier models since GPT-3.5. They show log-perplexity falling ~7 times faster since early 2026 than over 2022-2025. We think sharing pretraining loss is very valuable for improving public understanding of AI R
title_en: OpenAI published the pretraining loss of all of its frontier models since GPT-3.5. They show log-perplexity falling ~7 times faster since early 2026 than over 2022-2025. We think sharing pretraining loss is very valuable for improving public understanding of AI R
title_zh: OpenAI公布GPT-3.5以来预训练损失趋势
author: @METR_Evals
summary_en: OpenAI disclosed the pretraining loss data for all frontier models since GPT-3.5. Data indicates that since early 2026, the log-perplexity reduction rate has accelerated by approximately 7 times compared to the 2022-2025 period, signaling a significant leap in pretraining efficiency.
summary_zh: OpenAI发布了自GPT-3.5以来的前沿模型预训练损失数据，显示2026年后模型性能提升速度较2022-2025年有显著加速。
full_text_zh: OpenAI 公布了自 GPT-3.5 以来其所有前沿模型的预训练损失。他们显示，自 2026 年初以来，对数困惑度的下降速度比 2022 年至 2025 年期间快约 7 倍。我们认为分享预训练损失对于提高公众对 AI R 的理解非常有价值

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI公开披露了GPT-3.5及后续所有前沿模型的预训练损失（Pretraining Loss）数据。数据显示，自2026年初以来，对数困惑度（log-perplexity）的下降速率比2022至2025年期间提升了约7倍，显示出预训练效率在近年来实现了跨越式增长。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI disclosed the pretraining loss data for all frontier models since GPT-3.5. Data indicates that since early 2026, the log-perplexity reduction rate has accelerated by approximately 7 times compared to the 2022-2025 period, signaling a significant leap in pretraining efficiency.

elements_zh.where: 前沿模型技术披露
elements_zh.what: 公开GPT-3.5至今的预训练损失曲线数据
elements_zh.why: 旨在提升公众对AI研发进展与规模效应的科学认知

elements_en.what: Public release of pretraining loss curves since GPT-3.5
elements_en.why: Enhancing public understanding of AI development progress and scaling laws

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 预训练损失下降斜率的陡增，不仅反映了算力基础设施的规模红利，更预示着新型算法架构与数据效率优化已进入正反馈周期。对于行业竞争对手而言，这种效率倍增意味着单纯依赖算力投入的追赶门槛正在极速提高，市场格局向高效率研发范式倾斜。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The sharp increase in the slope of pretraining loss decline reflects not only the scale dividends of computational infrastructure but also the positive feedback cycle of novel architectural algorithms and data efficiency. For competitors, this efficiency surge implies that the barrier to entry for catch-up strategies based solely on compute investment is rising rapidly.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic现任及前任员工在近期交流中明确指出，在实现通用人工智能（AGI）的道路上，人类工程师的技术积累与工程实践仍存在巨大缺口。该观点旨在缓解行业对AI自动化导致的职业焦虑，号召技术人员将精力聚焦于AGI对齐这一核心工程难题。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Current and former Anthropic employees have emphasized that there remains a significant gap in engineering and technical execution on the path to AGI. This perspective seeks to alleviate professional anxiety regarding AI automation by redirecting technical efforts toward the critical challenge of AGI alignment.

elements_zh.where: 近期行业交流活动
elements_zh.what: 强调人类工程师在解决AGI对齐与复杂工程化难题中具备不可替代性
elements_zh.why: 应对AI自动化引发的行业就业焦虑，界定人类在AI演进中的核心价值

elements_en.what: Highlighting the irreplaceable role of human engineers in AGI alignment and complex engineering
elements_en.why: To address industry anxiety over automation and define the core value of human labor in AI evolution

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 单纯的算法迭代已非通往AGI的唯一瓶颈，系统架构与对齐机制的底层工程实现正成为稀缺能力。企业需警惕过度依赖自动化模型开发，忽视了将复杂工程路径与人类专家判断逻辑深度耦合的能力构建。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Algorithmic iteration is no longer the sole bottleneck to AGI, as the engineering implementation of system architecture and alignment mechanisms has become a scarce capability. Enterprises must guard against over-reliance on automated model development at the expense of integrating human expert judgment into complex engineering pipelines.

战略方向：从被动担忧AI替代转向参与定义AI架构
key_points_en: Core demand: Encouraging developers to focus on AGI alignment research
Current status: Shortage of human engineering capacity hindering AGI deployment
Strategic outlook: Shifting from fear of displacement to defining AI architecture
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 单纯的算法迭代已非通往AGI的唯一瓶颈，系统架构与对齐机制的底层工程实现正成为稀缺能力。企业需警惕过度依赖自动化模型开发，忽视了将复杂工程路径与人类专家判断逻辑深度耦合的能力构建。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Algorithmic iteration is no longer the sole bottleneck to AGI, as the engineering implementation of system architecture and alignment mechanisms has become a scarce capability. Enterprises must guard against over-reliance on automated model development at the expense of integrating human expert judgment into complex engineering pipelines.

title: GPT-6 for designing new protein shapes and sequences — no bio-specific model required. Another example of the unreasonable effectiveness of reasoning and code to solve problems universally.
title_en: GPT-6 for designing new protein shapes and sequences — no bio-specific model required. Another example of the unreasonable effectiveness of reasoning and code to solve problems universally.
title_zh: GPT-6展示跨领域蛋白质设计能力
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI researchers demonstrated that GPT-6 can design protein shapes and sequences without bio-specific training, leveraging its core reasoning and code generation capabilities. This signals a transition in AGI from task-specific models to cross-domain scientific problem-solving.
summary_zh: OpenAI研究人员披露GPT-6无需专用生物模型，即可通过通用逻辑推理实现蛋白质形态与序列的高效设计。
full_text_zh: GPT-6 用于设计新的蛋白质形状和序列——无需生物特异性模型。推理和代码普遍解决问题的不合理有效性的另一个例子。
full_text_en: GPT-6 for designing new protein shapes and sequences — no bio-specific model required. Another example of the unreasonable effectiveness of reasoning and code to solve problems universally.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI研究人员证实GPT-6在无需垂直领域模型辅助的情况下，通过底层逻辑推理与代码生成能力，成功实现蛋白质形态建模与序列设计。该进展标志着通用人工智能在复杂科学模拟领域实现从特定任务训练向跨模态推理的跨越。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI researchers demonstrated that GPT-6 can design protein shapes and sequences without bio-specific training, leveraging its core reasoning and code generation capabilities. This signals a transition in AGI from task-specific models to cross-domain scientific problem-solving.

elements_zh.where: AI前沿研发实验室
elements_zh.what: 无需生物专用模型，利用GPT-6的通用逻辑推理进行蛋白质设计
elements_zh.why: 验证大模型逻辑推理能力在复杂科学工程领域的泛化潜力

elements_en.what: Protein design using GPT-6 general reasoning, bypassing the need for bio-specific models
elements_en.why: To demonstrate the generalization of logical reasoning in complex scientific domains

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此现象证明大模型正在摆脱对高昂垂类数据清洗的依赖，凭借基础推理与代码模拟能力的Scaling效应实现科学发现。这预示着计算机生物学领域将迎来通用智能范式的范式转移，即通过逻辑求解器取代单一任务的预测模型。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This development suggests that Large Language Models are bypassing the reliance on expensive domain-specific data, leveraging scaling laws in reasoning to drive scientific discovery. It points toward a paradigm shift in computational biology where general-purpose logic solvers replace single-task predictive models.

title_en: ⚡ How did gRPC in LMCache go from slower than ZMQ to 1,617 RPCs per second against ZMQ's 1,322? Both numbers come from one run that replayed recorded vLLM engine requests against a saturated LMCache server. The vLLM engines on a node usual
title_zh: LMCache通过优化gRPC超越ZMQ性能
author: @lmcache
summary_en: LMCache has optimized its communication layer, achieving 1,617 RPCs per second via gRPC, outperforming ZMQ's 1,322 RPCs per second. The benchmark, conducted using replayed vLLM engine requests under saturation, demonstrates significant gains in inference throughput efficiency.
summary_zh: LMCache通过架构调优，使gRPC处理效率以1,617 RPC/s超过ZMQ的1,322 RPC/s。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 分布式推理缓存架构LMCache通过重构其通信协议栈，成功使gRPC接口在饱和负载下的处理能力达到每秒1,617次远程过程调用（RPCs），显著超过了原有的ZMQ（零消息队列）协议实现的1,322次/秒。该测试基于vLLM推理引擎在饱和环境下的压力重放，验证了针对高吞吐量推理场景下的协议优化成效。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: LMCache has optimized its communication layer, achieving 1,617 RPCs per second via gRPC, outperforming ZMQ's 1,322 RPCs per second. The benchmark, conducted using replayed vLLM engine requests under saturation, demonstrates significant gains in inference throughput efficiency.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Bottlenecks in inference serving have shifted from pure computation to distributed synchronization and scheduling. LMCache's protocol optimization highlights that communication overhead is now a critical variable in throughput, directly impacting unit costs in multi-node vLLM deployments.

article_content:
According to a post shared by Soumith Chintala citing Thinking Machines on X, early testing indicates NVIDIA Vera CPUs outperform Grace with strong sandbox workload scaling for agentic AI servers.

NVIDIA delivered a Vera CPU server to Thinking Machines for agentic AI workloads, according to a post by Soumith Chintala on November 24, 2026, citing early testing feedback from the company's compute team.

Vera CPUs represent a solid upgrade from Grace in initial benchmarks, with sandbox workloads scaling effectively to support faster iteration in AI agent development and reshape testing workflows for developers focused on agentic systems.

Cofounded and lead Pytorch at Meta. Also dabble in robotics at NYU.

article_content:
Kling AI Launches Kling Image 4.0 with Photographic Realism and Native 8K Generation Tweet

Beijing,China, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Kling AI, the AI-powered creative platform, today announced the launch of Kling Image 4.0, its latest image generation model that combines photographic realism, native 8K output, advanced text generation, and the ability to generate up to 10 cohesive images from a single prompt.

Designed for everyday creators and professionals in filmmaking, advertising, marketing, and design, the model also offers improved instruction following and more precise control over image composition, able to help creators to turn complex briefs into individual images or complete visual sets.

According to the latest Artificial Analysis image leaderboard, Kling Image 4.0 Preview maintains a leading position in both text-to-image and image editing. Its text-to-image capabilities rank third in the UIUX Design scenarios, according to the leaderboard.

Kling Image 4.0 creates images with the natural look of photographs that are taken straight from the camera, combining soft lighting, lifelike textures, and fine detail. The generated image can capture subtle human facial expressions and renders subjects that fit naturally into their surroundings.

In group portraits, the model produces greater variation in facial features, body types, ages, and poses to avoid the common issue in image genertion - that all people look identical. This gives creators more flexibility to develop diverse casts and visually expressive scenes.

Kling Image 4.0 for the first time in the industry supports AI image generation with native 8K resolution. It renders fine details across skin, fabric, product materials, and landscapes, so that intricate details remain sharp even in close-up views and extensive cropping, making it well suited for professional visual production.

The higher-resolution output also supports a range of professional applications, from digital campaigns and product imagery to large-format displays and outdoor advertising.

Kling Image 4.0 introduces enhanced text rendering, pairing clear, legible text with expressive layouts. It supports generating up to 2,000 characters in a single image and integrates text with other visual elements, maintaining clarity even for small text in posters. Creators can also edit text content and font styles within generated images to match their creative vision.

The built-in font library offers over 70 preset fonts, and creators can also upload font reference images to guide the desired style. From artistic lettering to multi-level poster layouts, Kling Image 4.0 precisely follows instructions for text placement, typography, and visual effects, bringing text and imagery together in cohesive designs.

Kling Image 4.0 further improves its multilingual capabilities, supporting text generation in English, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, simplified Chinese and traditional Chinese. This opens up more possibilities for text-based visual creation across languages.

With a single prompt, creators can generate a set of up to 10 related images. Kling Image 4.0 interprets the overall brief and plans the set as a whole, maintaining a consistent visual style and subject identity while varying framing, camera angles, and content. This reduces the need to generate and adjust each image individually.

The model adapts the set to the task: planning shots and narrative flow for storyboards, showcasing product angles and key selling points for e-commerce, and organizing layouts and information across presentation visuals.

Kling Image 4.0 also supports the creation of long-form e-commerce product pages and brand website visuals, combining product imagery, key information and brand elements into cohesive layouts. Text and images can be edited on separate layers, making revisions easier.

The launch of Kling Image 4.0 follows the recent launch of Kling 4.0, its latest video generation model featuring major improvements in visual realism, creative control and narrative coherence. From single image to complete visual sets, Kling Image 4.0 brings AI image generation closer to production-grade delivery, enabling creators in film, advertising, and marketing to turn ambitious ideas into finished work with consistency and speed.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 去中心化计算平台Phala Network推出了针对推理优化设计的DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017版本，具备“基座模型”与“无审查变体”双模态切换能力。该模型利用FP8精度技术，旨在帮助推理服务提供商在共享GPU算力资源受限的情况下，通过单引擎架构高效满足不同用户对合规性与响应灵活性差异化的需求。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Phala Network released the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 variant, featuring dual-mode switching between base and uncensored models. Optimized for FP8 precision, the architecture enables inference providers to fulfill diverse user requirements on shared GPU resources through a single engine.

elements_zh.where: 共享GPU算力推理服务平台
elements_zh.what: 发布DeepSeek V4.1 Flash，支持基座/无审查双模态切换
elements_zh.why: 降低推理服务提供商的算力部署复杂度，提升服务灵活性

elements_en.what: Released DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with dual-mode (base/uncensored) switching
elements_en.why: Reducing deployment complexity and increasing flexibility for inference providers

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Phala的方案揭示了推理市场向“算力资产精细化运营”的转型，通过模型变体封装降低了运维侧的冷启动与显存开销，这对于碎片化的分布式GPU供应网络至关重要。将无审查模型与标准基座集成于单引擎，本质上是在合规性边界内实现对边缘算力池最大化效能挖掘的策略选择。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Phala's approach reveals the shift toward precise management of compute assets in the inference market. By encapsulating model variants, it reduces cold-start overhead, which is critical for fragmented distributed GPU networks. Integrating uncensored variants with base models within a single engine is a strategic move to maximize efficiency within existing compute pools.

Reduced memory and compute overhead for inference providers managing multiple model versions.

title: Really excited about this one. MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box.
title_en: Really excited about this one. MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box.
title_zh: 对此真的很兴奋。 MCP 服务器现在可以附带自己的技能，因此 Claude Code 知道如何开箱即用地使用它们。
author: @bcherny
summary_en: Anthropic has launched the public beta of Skills over MCP, enabling AI agents to utilize step-by-step guides and best practices alongside external tool access. Features like Tasks for background processing and Elicitation for user input confirmation have also reached general availability, aiming to upgrade Claude's capabilities from single-task execution to complex workflow orchestration.
summary_zh: Anthropic发布Skills over MCP测试版，允许AI Agent获取多步骤操作手册，显著提升Claude协作能力。
article_content:
Anthropic has opened Skills over MCP in public beta, letting apps that connect to Claude ship playbooks alongside their tools. Tasks, for long background jobs, and Elicitation, which pauses for user input, are now generally available, with File Uploads coming soon.

Apps that plug into Claude through MCP can now also tell it how to use them, Anthropic said on Tuesday. The feature, Skills over MCP, is in public beta in Claude and Claude Code.

MCP is the open standard Anthropic launched two years ago to link AI agents to outside apps and data. Servers built on it already list the tools Claude can use. With skills, they can also ship step-by-step guides and best practices, which Claude loads only when needed.

Shopify uses skills to help Claude design and update online stores, and HubSpot to onboard customers. Skills update with the server, so users have nothing extra to install. More apps are opening up, too: Canva opened its MCP server to all developers on Tuesday.

The beta is on by default for Pro, Max and Ultra plans. Team admins can switch it on, and Enterprise support is coming soon.

Two other features are now generally available. Tasks lets a server run long jobs in the background while Claude keeps working, which ZoomInfo uses for deeper research. Elicitation lets a server pause and ask the user for input.

GitHub, for example, makes users type a repository’s name before an agent deletes it. Supabase confirms costs before creating a paid project. A fourth feature, File Uploads, will soon let Claude send PDFs, spreadsheets and images to servers.

The features are part of MCP, so servers that support them also work in other compatible apps. Anthropic says MCP now sees over 700M SDK downloads a month. In August, OpenAI and four rivals agreed on a standard for packaging skills and MCP servers.

Skills carry risks, too. That same month, researchers found malicious agent skills that stole passwords and keys after about 1.7 million installs.

full_text_en: Really excited about this one. MCP servers can now ship with their own skills, so Claude Code knows how to use them out of the box.
article_content_zh:
Anthropic在MCP协议中引入技能后，Shopify等平台已开始利用该功能设计并自动更新在线商店，HubSpot则利用其辅助客户入驻流程。技能随服务器同步更新，无需用户额外手动安装。

此外，该更新涉及的安全与合规机制包含Elicitation，要求AI在执行删除数据或金融交易等敏感任务前必须暂停并征得用户二次确认。目前该Beta功能已在Claude Pro、Max及Ultra订阅用户中默认开启。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Anthropic正式发布Skills over MCP功能的公测版，使AI Agent不仅能调用外部工具，还能加载多步骤执行手册与最佳实践。同时，Tasks（后台任务）与Elicitation（用户反馈确认）功能也已全面开放，该套件旨在通过标准化协议将Claude的自主协作能力从单一任务处理升级至复杂工作流编排。

Features like Tasks for background processing and Elicitation for user input confirmation have also reached general availability, aiming to upgrade Claude's capabilities from single-task execution to complex workflow orchestration.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Anthropic通过Skills over MCP确立了AI Agent编排层面的事实标准，其核心逻辑是将‘隐性的过程逻辑’显性化为可随SDK分发的标准化组件。这种将“操作手册”嵌入工具集的操作，直接降低了开发者维护Agent执行策略的复杂度，对于构建端到端闭环的AI生产力工具具有决定性意义。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By introducing Skills over MCP, Anthropic is establishing a de facto standard for AI agent orchestration by codifying 'implicit process logic' into distributable, standardized components. Embedding 'manuals' directly into toolsets significantly reduces development friction for agentic strategies and is critical for building end-to-end, autonomous AI productivity systems.

title: Introducing WebMCP support in AI SDK. Use the new WebMCP transport with our MCP client to discover and call tools exposed by your website.
title_en: Introducing WebMCP support in AI SDK. Use the new WebMCP transport with our MCP client to discover and call tools exposed by your website.
title_zh: 谷歌推出WebMCP协议，重构AI智能体网页交互标准
author: @aisdk
summary_en: Google has introduced WebMCP (Web Model Context Protocol) within its AI SDK, aiming to replace brittle visual-based web interactions with structured, machine-readable interfaces. By allowing websites to expose specific actions and data directly to AI agents, the protocol shifts web navigation from visual imitation to explicit API-like execution.
summary_zh: 谷歌在Chrome浏览器中引入WebMCP预览功能，允许网站直接向AI智能体暴露结构化数据与可执行工具。
article_content:
Google is taking a step toward formalizing how artificial intelligence (AI) agents interact with the web, introducing WebMCP as an early preview feature inside Chrome.

WebMCP, short for Web Model Context Protocol, enables websites to expose structured data (like product listings and availability) and defined, machine-readable actions directly to AI systems. Instead of parsing HTML and guessing where buttons or forms are located, agents can invoke clearly defined actions inside the browser. In effect, Chrome becomes a controlled layer where tasks such as searching inventory, initiating checkout or submitting service requests are handled through explicit calls rather than visual interpretation.

If adopted at scale, the model could reshape how commerce, customer support and other digital services manage agent-driven activity. By shifting from imitation to structured access, WebMCP aims to make automated interactions more reliable while giving businesses clearer oversight of how their data, pricing and workflows are accessed and executed.

Under the traditional model, AI agents operate much like robotic users. They scan a webpage, identify fields and buttons, and simulate clicks. When a checkout flow changes or a class name is modified, the automation may fail. That fragility limits reliability for enterprise use cases.

WebMCP introduces a system in which websites define the actions they want to expose, such as “search inventory,” “initiate checkout,” or “submit support request.” Agents then call those actions directly through Chrome, rather than reconstructing intent from visual layout. VentureBeat described the approach as turning every website into a structured tool for agents, while Forbes framed it as a browser-based backbone for the agentic web, where agents do more work for users.

Instead of blocking bots outright or tolerating scraping, companies can determine which capabilities are accessible, what data is returned, and how transactions are attributed. That structure may reduce server strain from scraping traffic and create clearer audit trails for agent-driven interactions.

The move also aligns with Google’s broader push into agent-driven commerce. Google introduced an Agent Payments Protocol, which is aimed at standardizing how AI agents handle transactions, according to PYMNTS and Google’s own Cloud blog. WebMCP extends that logic from payments to general web interaction, suggesting a coordinated effort to formalize agent access across the digital stack.

If AI agents become regular participants in commerce, reliability and attribution will matter. In travel, an agent booking a flight must access live pricing, seat availability and payment flows without error. In eCommerce, an agent comparing products or completing a checkout must handle promotions, inventory updates and identity verification accurately. In customer support, agents may retrieve account data or trigger service actions on behalf of users.

Hypothetical use case: a pharmacy chain wants to let assistants help with refills without letting bots scrape account pages. With WebMCP, the pharmacy could expose a limited set of actions like “find prescription,” “check nearby stock,” “schedule pickup” and “submit insurance info.” A patient asks, “Refill my allergy medication at the closest store before 6 p.m.” The agent calls those actions through Chrome, receives structured results and completes the request without guessing which button to press.

Scraping-based systems can struggle with those tasks at scale. They may misinterpret page elements, miss hidden constraints or fail silently. By contrast, a WebMCP-based interaction offers defined inputs and outputs, reducing ambiguity.

Attribution is another potential shift. Today, when an AI agent drives traffic or completes a purchase, businesses may see only generic browser activity. With structured agent pathways, companies could better identify agent-originated transactions and measure their performance. That data may influence pricing models, partnerships and marketing strategies as agent-driven discovery grows.

Adoption remains an open question. Websites must opt in by exposing structured actions, and enterprises will evaluate security, governance and competitive implications. WebMCP does not eliminate APIs, nor does it instantly end scraping. If the model gains traction, the web may evolve into a dual-layer environment, one optimized for people and another for autonomous agents operating with defined permissions.

PYMNTS reported that the next phase of AI agents depends on the infrastructure beneath them, specifically the shift toward API-first architectures (systems built around stable interfaces) and structured execution layers.

article_content_zh:
WebMCP旨在将网站直接转化为智能体可操作的工具链，改变过去智能体需通过DOM解析与屏幕模拟进行交互的低效模式。这标志着浏览器从单纯的内容渲染器转变为智能代理的交互枢纽。

通过该架构，企业能够精准定义允许智能体访问的数据与动作接口（如库存查询、交易下单），这不仅能显著降低因UI布局变动导致自动化中断的频率，还为企业提供了细粒度的流量审计轨迹，从而实现从“被动防御”到“主动赋能”的AI流量治理升级。

title_en: the most popular personal AI agent for each state (my best guess)
title_zh: 每个州最受欢迎的个人人工智能代理（我的最佳猜测）
author: @DavidPawlan
summary_zh: 继本月早些时候 Meta 重磅发布 Muse AI 代理之后，OpenAI 于周二凭借 Dots 进军个人代理市场，为人工智能市场的下一场大战奠定了基础。在其年度 DevDay 开发者大会上，OpenAI 将 Dots 描述为“永远在线”
article_content:
Following Meta's blockbuster release of its Muse AI agent earlier this month, OpenAI jumped into the personal agent market on Tuesday with Dots, setting the stage for what could be the next big battle in the artificial intelligence market.

At its annual DevDay developer conference, OpenAI described Dots as "always-on"agents designed to help users complete a range of tasks. Since the release of Muse three weeks ago, investors have rallied around Meta, sending the stock up 29% in September, on pace for its best month since 2013.

That level of enthusiasm underscores the power of personal agents and the promise that consumers and office workers will be able to use the technology to book travel, pay bills, respond to emails and perform many more tasks. But OpenAI's entry, arriving soon after the launch of Muse, serves as a reminder that the AI market includes a handful of large companies all converging around the same types of products with little ability to lock in users.

Google calls its Gemini Spark offering "your 24/7 personal AI agent"for help, and Apple is trying to step up its position in the AI battle with its redesigned Siri AI, which it describes as "a profoundly more capable and personal assistant."

"I think what we are watching is an inevitable evolution of the technology,"said John Waldmann, CEO of HR tech startup Homebase and a user of various AI agent-related tools. "It's probably no surprise that it's all happening around the same time."

It's not just the big companies that see the opportunity.

AI assistant startup Instinct announced Monday that it raised $1 billion from venture firms including Sequoia at a $10 billion valuation. And another startup, Town, is reportedly looking at a $1 billion valuation.

Town CEO Jean-Denis Grèze told CNBC in a statement that OpenAI's debut of Dots, "continues to validate the category and the need for work assistants."

"It's been our focus at Town from the very beginning,"Grèze said, adding that he welcomes the competition.

On Tuesday, all eyes were on OpenAI, as investors and AI enthusiasts anticipated what the ChatGPT creator would unveil in the wake of last week's Meta Connect developer conference. There, Meta announced forthcoming AI devices, including a pendant, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg called Muse the "centerpiece"of the company's AI strategy.

Taking the stage in San Francisco for DevDay, Altman called Dots "remarkably capable"and "built to handle really anything you can think of."Although developers could already use OpenAI's existing tools to manage scores of AI agents for various office tasks, Dots promises to be an easier way for workers to use powerful digital assistants to help with tools like Slack and Microsoft Teams.

### More uplifting than AI safety

The rush of new agents hitting the market offers a more uplifting story for AI companies at a time when the leading labs are facing intensifying scrutiny due to emerging concerns that the most advanced models are at risk of spinning out of human control.

On Tuesday, as Altman was attending DevDay, his second-in-command, Greg Brockman, was in Washington for a lunch that President Donald Trump was hosting for top technology leaders. The topic was AI safety, and the event came more than two weeks after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei sent shock waves across the industry, writing an essay urging AI companies to slow the pace of frontier model development.

Nick Deveau, CEO of AI sales startup GrottoAI, is a fan of AI agent tools like Instinct and sees the vision as companies start building them for a wider audience.

"The interesting thing about all of these, which I think has become apparent really quickly and is evidenced by some of the valuations, is that people see this as the first successful proof point of true agentic work hitting consumers,"Deveau said.

There's still the question of whether consumers will pay. Meta's Muse is free with a usage limit and can be purchased starting at $20 a month after that. OpenAI's Dots is only available starting at the $100 per month Pro plan and higher.

And even with Muse racking up millions of downloads across app stores, that doesn't mean people are actively using it or other AI agents, Waldmann said.

"People will try it, but is it really adding value?"Waldmann said. "Is it part of a daily habit?"

Thomas Randall, a research director at the Info-Tech Research Group, said in an email that "the race is on,"as AI companies search to figure out how consumers want to use agents and what will keep them coming back.

"Once leading systems are broadly capable, the winner will likely be determined by which agent is the easiest to adopt, the most connected, and the hardest to leave,"Randall said. "We'll see who's distribution will gather steam first."
