full_text_zh: 今天，我们将与 Google Cloud Agent Gateway 一起全面提供 Workspace MCP 服务器和 Workspace CLI。传统的 REST API 是为人性化的应用程序构建的。现在，AI 代理通过 DLP 检查获得进入工作区的标准路径
full_text_en: We are making Workspace MCP servers and the Workspace CLI generally available today, alongside Google Cloud Agent Gateway. Traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced apps. Now AI agents get a standard path into Workspace with DLP checks
article_content:
AI-generated illustration Key Points Google now treats autonomous agents as a distinct security class requiring policy…View moreGoogle now treats autonomous agents as a distinct security class requiring policy checks and human confirmation.Third-party agent platforms face a compliance deadline as the Workspace AI Tools Addendum bans circumventing MCP.Agent Gateway enforces default-deny outbound rules and screens traffic for indirect prompt injection. Google announced on November 24, 2026 that its Workspace Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers and Workspace command-line interface (CLI) are generally available, alongside rules requiring AI agents to use those interfaces instead of existing REST APIs. Technical enforcement begins February 1, 2027.

Google reports that Workspace APIs handle more than 2.8 trillion calls a month, with public Drive API traffic more than two-and-a-half times its 2022 volume. Traditional applications can continue using existing REST APIs; the new requirement applies to AI agents and other AI-driven tools.

Google’s rationale is that traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced applications, where a valid OAuth token implied user intent. An autonomous agent acting at machine speed across email, documents and cloud infrastructure changes that assumption. The new design puts policy checks, data boundaries and human confirmation into the request path.

The Workspace servers use MCP to give AI applications a standard way to read data and take actions. Dedicated remote servers are generally available for Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Chat and Tasks, inheriting each user’s permissions and data-governance controls. The Workspace CLI serves local agents, terminal workflows and automation, with structured JSON output and scoped OAuth sign-in across Workspace services.

Each agent call through these interfaces is checked against organizational permissions, data-loss-prevention rules and classification labels. The MCP servers reject OAuth clients that are not designated for AI agents, and agents connecting to Workspace must use dedicated OAuth client IDs with least-privilege scopes and usage quotas. Billing is scheduled to begin on April 1, 2027, while time-limited approvals are listed as coming soon.

Draft creation and document summarization can run autonomously. Sending email, changing Drive sharing permissions and making bulk edits require explicit user confirmation. Workspace administrators can view, audit and revoke agents in the admin console; user-facing activity review and revocation, plus controls to block agent access to Gmail messages and specific Drive files or folders, remain forthcoming.

The Workspace AI Tools Addendum covers standalone agents, the software harnesses that deploy or orchestrate them, and applications or services using AI models. It bars disguising a tool to avoid classification or circumvent the Google MCP requirement. That makes the migration a compliance issue for third-party agent platforms as well as for developers building directly on Workspace.

Workspace user data and Google Technical Information, a category of service information obtained or derived through Workspace access points, may be processed only to fulfill active, user-authorized tasks. Neither category can be used for model training, fine-tuning, evaluation dataset construction, model distillation or developing a service similar to a Workspace service. Scraping and systematic probing beyond what an authorized task requires are also prohibited.

Google Technical Information cannot be stored for more than 30 days. Covered user data and technical information must not be retained after a tool is disconnected or its access is revoked. If Google reasonably believes those rules have been violated, it can immediately restrict or remove the tool’s access, or suspend or terminate the customer’s access to the relevant Workspace services.

On Google Cloud, Agent Gateway verifies Agent Identities against the Agent Registry directory, enforces identity and access management policies and default-deny outbound rules, and screens requests with Model Armor. It governs inbound client-to-agent traffic and outbound requests from agents to tools, APIs and other agents. Custom authorization checks can be delegated to an organization’s own policy engine or third-party security tools through Service Extensions.

Cloud Run support and Agent Gateway for cross-cloud Kubernetes environments remain in Limited Preview. Each gateway instance can govern up to 5,000 resources registered in Agent Registry.

Google’s MCP configuration guide requires screening prompts and responses for indirect prompt injection, meaning hidden instructions in untrusted content, using Model Armor or a documented alternative. Malicious emails or documents could hijack a session and modify, steal or delete data. Current known issues include some English-only approval prompts, no user self-service viewing or revocation of saved tool approvals, and expiration of those approvals after 90 days.

For enterprises, agent governance is now built into the supported Workspace access path. The practical burden is the migration: existing agent integrations must satisfy the new identity, confirmation, screening and retention rules on Google’s schedule, while parts of the user-control and deployment model remain pending.

summary_zh: 谷歌正式发布Workspace MCP服务器与CLI工具，强制要求AI代理通过专用网关接入，以实现合规性审核与DLP数据泄露防护。
summary_en: Google announced the general availability of Workspace MCP servers and CLI on November 24, 2026, mandating that AI agents use these interfaces for interaction. Effective February 1, 2027, this shift forces agents to operate through an Agent Gateway with built-in DLP and audit capabilities, treating agents as a distinct security classification.
article_content_zh:
谷歌通过Agent Gateway重新定义了企业工作区的数据交互权限。传统的REST API在处理人类行为时具备有效的OAuth令牌保障，但面对高速、自动化的AI代理时，其安全边界显得极为脆弱。新的MCP接口直接在请求路径上集成了DLP审查和人工确认流程。

该协议将Gmail、Drive、Docs、Sheets等服务封装为受控节点。AI代理在调用这些服务时，必须使用专用的OAuth客户端ID，且在执行敏感操作（如发送邮件、修改Drive权限、批量编辑文档）时，必须获得用户明确确认。此举实际上将第三方代理彻底纳入了谷歌云的安全合规监控网格内。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 谷歌于2026年11月24日宣布全面推出Workspace MCP（模型上下文协议）服务器与CLI，并规定AI代理需摒弃传统REST API，转而通过具备DLP检查与审计功能的Agent Gateway接入工作区数据。该举措自2027年2月1日起正式强制执行，旨在将AI代理定义为需严格权限管控的新型安全类别。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Google announced the general availability of Workspace MCP servers and CLI on November 24, 2026, mandating that AI agents use these interfaces for interaction. Effective February 1, 2027, this shift forces agents to operate through an Agent Gateway with built-in DLP and audit capabilities, treating agents as a distinct security classification.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 这是全球首个将AI代理合规治理从软件层拉入协议层的重大举措，标志着谷歌通过控制数据链路底层协议，实质性垄断了企业级AI代理的操作标准。通过强制调用MCP，谷歌不仅防范了提示词注入，更将数据权限边界直接植入代理的执行逻辑，迫使第三方代理平台必须服从其统一的安全审计框架。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This is a seminal move to shift AI agent governance from software-level to protocol-level, effectively enabling Google to set the standard for enterprise agent interactions. By mandating MCP, Google mitigates prompt injection risks while embedding data governance directly into execution logic, forcing third-party platforms to comply with its proprietary security auditing framework.

title_en: Speed up Qwen3.8-27B with our new DFlash2 speculator model. ⚡️ Up to 7 draft tokens per step 📈 4.5 avg acceptance length on HumanEval, 6.0 on Math Reasoning 🔥 Up to 2.76× output throughput vs. baseline on summarization & 2.68× on RAG (Speedbe
title_zh: 使用我们新的 DFlash2 投机器模型加速 Qwen3.8-27B。 ⚡️ 每步最多 7 个草稿令牌 📈 HumanEval 上的平均接受长度为 4.5，数学推理上的平均接受长度为 6.0 🔥 相对于汇总的基线，输出吞吐量高达 2.76×；RAG 上的输出吞吐量为 2.68×（Speedbe）
author: @RedHat_AI
summary_zh: 据 𝕏 (Twitter) 报道（技术焦点：代码工程增强）：使用我们新的 DFlash2 投机器模型加速 Qwen3.8-27B。 ⚡️ 每步最多 7 个草稿令牌 📈 HumanEval 上的平均接受长度为 4.5，数学推理上的平均接受长度为 6.0 🔥 相对于汇总的基线，输出吞吐量高达 2.76×；RAG 上的输出吞吐量为 2.68×（Speedbe），更多技术实测与行业影响持续跟踪。

title_en: The future is custom models for maximum performance, cost and ownership thanks to open-source! Last week, we released Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted (that became second most trending on HF) and a bunch of harness-adapted models that drastically improve
title_zh: 未来是通过开源实现最大性能、成本和所有权的定制模型！上周，我们发布了 Qwen3.8-27B-pi-adapted（成为 HF 上第二热门的
author: Clément Delangue
author_role: Hugging Face 联合创始人兼 CEO

ai_analysis.insight_en: The frontier of enterprise AI is shifting from sheer parameter scaling to domain-specific fine-tuning and inference optimization. This case proves that post-training open-weight models provides a superior ROI path compared to relying solely on massive closed-source APIs.

ai_analysis.insight_en: Small-parameter models are rapidly outperforming general-purpose LLMs in specific vertical tasks like OCR, underscoring industry preference for specialized inference pipelines. author: @yukez
summary_en: Professor Yuke Zhu, an expert in robot perception and learning, is set to join the Department of Computer Science at Princeton University in the fall of 2027. He will relocate his existing Robot Perception and Learning Lab to the university and initiate a new recruitment cycle for PhD candidates.

title: So much of the US social-political contract is 'line must go up' in the stock market, and so much of the stock market now is predicated on 'AI must work.' And AI is intensely politically unpopular. Seems like a big tension.

title: 有人为 Snapp 游乐设施构建了一个非官方的 MCP 服务器。它可以在一个未记录的 API 上运行，包括实时驱动程序和所有内容，但随时可能会崩溃。我以另一种方式构建了 TADA 和 Throo。特意开，0%佣金，任何代理都可以叫真司机。尝试一下。告诉我什么
title_en: Someone built an unofficial MCP server for Snapp rides. It works, live driver and all, on an undocumented API that can break any day. I built TADA and Throo the other way. Open on purpose, 0% commission, any agent can call a real driver. Try it. Tell me what
title_zh: 开发者构建Snapp非官方MCP服务器
full_text_zh: 有人为 Snapp 游乐设施构建了一个非官方的 MCP 服务器。它可以在一个未记录的 API 上运行，包括实时驱动程序和所有内容，但随时可能会崩溃。我以另一种方式构建了 TADA 和 Throo。特意开，0%佣金，任何代理都可以叫真司机。尝试一下。告诉我什么
full_text_en: Someone built an unofficial MCP server for Snapp rides. It works, live driver and all, on an undocumented API that can break any day. I built TADA and Throo the other way. Open on purpose, 0% commission, any agent can call a real driver. Try it. Tell me what
summary_zh: 独立开发者通过逆向未记录的API接口，为Snapp平台构建了非官方MCP服务器以实现实时调度。
summary_en: An independent developer has built an unofficial MCP server for the Snapp platform by leveraging undocumented APIs to enable real-time driver access. While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 独立开发者利用Snapp平台未公开的底层API，开发了旨在接入Model Context Protocol（MCP）的第三方中间件。该实现通过抓取实时驱动程序数据进行交互，旨在打破封闭生态的调度限制，但因缺乏官方兼容性保障，存在极高的运行稳定性风险与接口封禁隐患。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: An independent developer has built an unofficial MCP server for the Snapp platform by leveraging undocumented APIs to enable real-time driver access. While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.

elements_zh.where: Snapp平台物流调度生态
elements_zh.what: 通过逆向未记录API实现非官方MCP接入与自定义调度逻辑
elements_zh.why: 寻求绕过官方平台限制实现更灵活的代理调度与零佣金机制

elements_en.what: Built unofficial MCP server using undocumented APIs for real-time driver control
elements_en.why: Attempting to circumvent platform commission and access proprietary scheduling workflows

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举揭示了基于AI Agent的MCP协议在物流垂直领域的渗透尝试，但通过逆向手段构建的核心组件难以进入生产环境。这种非授权的接口集成不仅面临法律合规的灰度挑战，更预示着平台方需进一步加固API鉴权以防御私自接入带来的安全漏洞。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This development highlights the push to integrate MCP into logistics, yet unofficial reverse-engineered integrations are structurally unfit for production. Platform owners must prioritize API security and authentication hardening to mitigate the risks associated with unauthorized agentic access.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 独立开发者利用Snapp平台未公开的底层API，开发了旨在接入Model Context Protocol（MCP）的第三方中间件。该实现通过抓取实时驱动程序数据进行交互，旨在打破封闭生态的调度限制，但因缺乏官方兼容性保障，存在极高的运行稳定性风险与接口封禁隐患。
ai_analysis.digest_en: An independent developer has built an unofficial MCP server for the Snapp platform by leveraging undocumented APIs to enable real-time driver access. While this integration facilitates third-party control over logistics, it faces significant stability risks and potential termination due to the lack of official API support.
key_points_zh: 核心动机：通过避开平台佣金实现代理自主调度
关键技术：基于未记录的Snapp API实现数据透传与驱动交互
行业风险：API变动会导致系统崩溃且存在违规调用风险
key_points_en: Motivation: Circumventing platform commissions for autonomous logistics
Technical detail: Leveraging undocumented APIs to bypass standard driver dispatch
Risk factors: High technical volatility and potential for permanent platform-side blocking

ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This development highlights the push to integrate MCP into logistics, yet unofficial reverse-engineered integrations are structurally unfit for production. ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此表态反映了美国民粹主义监管派对AI巨头垄断及资本泡沫的深层忧虑，预示着未来若发生科技板块连锁崩盘，政府层面的“救市压力”将遭遇严重的政治阻力。地缘与监管博弈已将AI基础设施的超额支出视为一种潜在的系统性金融负担，而非仅仅是技术竞争资产。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This stance highlights growing political anxiety regarding the systemic economic fragility caused by Big Tech's AI monopolization. Future financial crises triggered by a burst in AI capital expenditure will likely face significant legislative resistance to government bailouts, framing AI infrastructure as a potential liability rather than a national strategic asset.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 该分析对AI智能体生态中的提示词（Prompt）、技能（Skill）、模型上下文协议（MCP）及子智能体（Subagent）进行技术拆解。核心指出各类组件在提升任务处理能力的同时，均以消耗上下文窗口容量为代价，需根据任务复杂度在模块化扩展与推理成本间进行精确权衡。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: This analysis breaks down the four core modules in AI agent architecture: Prompts, Skills, MCP, and Subagents. elements_zh.where: AI智能体开发环境
elements_zh.what: 分析四种功能模块对上下文窗口的消耗差异
elements_zh.why: 优化智能体推理效率与上下文管理性能

elements_en.what: Evaluation of context consumption for four functional modules
elements_en.why: Optimizing agent inference efficiency and context management

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 智能体架构的本质是计算资源与语义精度的博弈，模型上下文协议（MCP）的引入将标准化接口数据，但在复杂任务链中，过度调用子智能体会导致显著的上下文污染与长文本损耗。开发者应优先将静态技能固化为工具函数，而非完全依赖长提示词注入，以维持高推理质量。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Agent architecture is fundamentally a trade-off between compute resources and semantic precision; while MCP standardizes interface data, excessive subagent invocation in complex chains leads to significant context degradation. Developers should prioritize encoding static skills as tool functions rather than relying on heavy prompt injection to maintain high inference quality.

elements_zh.where: 企业级或个人AI开发应用场景
elements_zh.what: 通过RAG架构接入本地文档，实现私有化大模型交互

elements_en.what: Private LLM interaction using RAG architecture for local documents
elements_en.why: Addressing demands for AI data privacy and custom knowledge management

ai_analysis.insight_zh: AnythingLLM这类工具反映了开发者对通用LLM产品化过程中隐私外泄的防御心态。这种围绕本地向量数据库与开源模型的部署方案，是企业在部署AI智能助手时绕过复杂合规审查、实现数据沙箱隔离的必要过渡方案。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Tools like AnythingLLM reflect a growing defensive posture regarding data leakage during the integration of general-purpose LLMs. Deployment models centered on local vector databases and open-source weights are the essential bridge for enterprises to bypass complex compliance hurdles while achieving data sandboxing for AI assistants.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 腾讯AI团队宣布开源Hy MT3机器翻译模型系列，包括1.8B、7B及30B-A3B等多种尺寸。该系列模型采用Apache 2.0协议，通过优化计算效率，在3B激活参数规模下即实现了超越同类超大规模计算模型的翻译质量，支持语言范围已覆盖38种。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Tencent AI has open-sourced the Hy MT3 machine translation model series, available in 1.8B, 7B, and 30B-A3B configurations under the Apache 2.0 license. The models demonstrate superior translation performance at a 3B active parameter count compared to significantly larger models, with current language coverage expanded to 38 languages.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 区块链项目Dfinity展示了集成方案，允许用户直接通过ChatGPT智能体指令完成云引擎（Cloud Engine）的创建与应用部署。该流程通过自然语言交互实现从基础设施配置到应用运行的自动化，全程无需切换移动端作业界面。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Dfinity demonstrated an integration allowing users to launch cloud engines and deploy applications directly via ChatGPT agents. This workflow enables full-stack automation from infrastructure configuration to application execution through natural language, eliminating the need to switch mobile interfaces.

elements_zh.where: ChatGPT交互界面
elements_zh.what: 通过AI智能体实现云引擎的启动与App部署
elements_zh.why: 降低云基础设施运维门槛，提升自动化编程部署效率

elements_en.what: Direct launch and deployment of cloud engines via AI agents
elements_en.why: Lowering entry barriers for cloud infrastructure management

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举标志着从“辅助代码编写”向“自动化基础设施运维”的范式转移，通过AI Agent打通了从逻辑代码到生产环境的物理隔阂。未来云原生平台的核心竞争点将从单纯的算力堆砌，转向API与大模型Agent的深度兼容性，以实现开发流程的彻底去中心化与智能化。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This signals a paradigm shift from assisted coding to automated infrastructure operations, bypassing the physical barrier between logical code and production environments. Competitive advantage in cloud-native platforms will shift from raw compute scale to deep API compatibility with LLM agents to enable fully automated, decentralized deployment cycles.

ai_analysis.digest_en: Dfinity demonstrated an integration allowing users to launch cloud engines and deploy applications directly via ChatGPT agents. This workflow enables full-stack automation from infrastructure configuration to application execution through natural language, eliminating the need to switch mobile interfaces.
key_points_zh: 利用ChatGPT接口直接调动底层基础设施
实现从环境启动到App上线的端到端AI自动化
降低分布式云计算平台的应用部署操作门槛
key_points_en: Integration of ChatGPT with underlying infrastructure APIs
End-to-end automation from environment startup to app deployment
Lowering operational barriers for distributed cloud platforms
ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: 此举标志着从“辅助代码编写”向“自动化基础设施运维”的范式转移，通过AI Agent打通了从逻辑代码到生产环境的物理隔阂。未来云原生平台的核心竞争点将从单纯的算力堆砌，转向API与大模型Agent的深度兼容性，以实现开发流程的彻底去中心化与智能化。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: This signals a paradigm shift from assisted coding to automated infrastructure operations, bypassing the physical barrier between logical code and production environments. Competitive advantage in cloud-native platforms will shift from raw compute scale to deep API compatibility with LLM agents to enable fully automated, decentralized deployment cycles.

title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 适合研究口味：
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 发布后，我看到评论表明一般基准测试的改进并不令人印象深刻。然而，对于旨在实现AGI或ASI的人工智能公司来说，真正重要的能力是什么？ 2026年11月24日，评估AI研发能力的P-Zero Research
article_content:
After the release of GPT-6.2 Astra, I saw comments suggesting that the improvements in general benchmarks were underwhelming. However, for AI companies aiming to achieve AGI or ASI, what are the truly important capabilities?

On November 24, 2026, P-Zero Research, which evaluates AI research and development capabilities, published some very interesting measurement results.

GPT-6.2 Astra's experimental research taste is 4.9 times that of the human experts who participated in the study. This is the highest figure measured among AI models to date. Anthropic's Fable 5.2 was 2.5 times.

What is noteworthy is that the capability being evaluated is not knowledge volume or coding ability, but Research Taste.

Is an excellent researcher someone with vast knowledge? Or is it someone who can process complex mathematical formulas at high speed? Of course, those are also important capabilities. However, in research that breaks new ground in unknown territories, a different set of skills is required.

Which problems are worth tackling? Which hypotheses are promising? What experiments will yield important information? And, what should be read from the experimental results, and what should be tried next?

P-Zero Research calls this ability Research Taste. Among these, the TasteVal benchmark was developed to measure the ability to design experiments and interpret results for given research tasks.

The metric used in this evaluation is the Compute Multiplier. It represents how much less computational resource is needed to achieve experimental results equivalent to those of a human expert.

Researcher Required GPU Time Human Expert 20 hours Fable 5.2 8 hours GPT-6.2 Astra approx. 4.1 hours

GPT-6.2 Astra is estimated to obtain equivalent results with about one-fifth of the experimental computational resources by efficiently selecting promising experiments.

However, this is not a comparison that includes the computational resources or costs required for the AI's own reasoning. Also, it does not mean that it has surpassed human intelligence in general by 4.9 times.

The evaluation method of TasteVal is very interesting. It separates the research and development process into two roles: Researcher and Coder.

The Researcher devises experiments and interprets the results. The Coder implements the code according to those instructions and executes the experiments on NVIDIA H100 GPUs. Then, the obtained results are reported to the Researcher. The Researcher devises the next experiment based on those results.

Both human researchers and AI models use a common Coder. In the original paper published in October 2026, Anthropic's Opus 4.8 was adopted as the Coder.

Eight types of tasks related to AI research and development were prepared for evaluation, including selection of pre-training data, language model training, fine-tuning, modeling of human preferences, and resistance to adversarial prompts.

From the human side, 24 experts with research experience at OpenAI, Google DeepMind, NVIDIA, Microsoft Research, the University of Oxford, and others participated. Moreover, the comparison benchmark is not the average of the participants, but the human expert who achieved the best results in each task.

Looking at the graph released this time, a change more interesting than the raw figures of GPT-6.2 Astra becomes apparent. Since the end of 2025, the rate of improvement in research taste has changed drastically.

In the original TasteVal paper published in October 2026, the following doubling periods were reported regarding the experimental research taste of state-of-the-art AI models.

Period Research Taste Doubling Period 2023–December 2025 Approx. 14 months After December 2025 Approx. 3 months

The vertical axis of the graph is on a logarithmic scale. In other words, what appears to be a linear rise actually represents exponential growth.

Of course, there is no guarantee that this trend will continue in the future. Furthermore, the paper does not confirm a similar acceleration for other metrics comparing final experimental results.

Nevertheless, the result that research capability to efficiently utilize computational resources is growing rapidly is something that cannot be overlooked when considering the future of AI.

In AI development to date, securing more GPUs and performing larger-scale computations has been a key means of improving performance. However, increasing GPUs requires semiconductor manufacturing, data center construction, power procurement, and enormous capital.

On the other hand, what if we could extract more research results from the same computational resources? It may be possible to accelerate research and development without increasing physical computational resources.

What can only be discovered after repeating experiments hundreds of times, a superior intelligence might discover in dozens of experiments. What is important is not just the ability to compute, but the ability to judge what should be computed.

In addition to scaling computational resources, the scaling of the intelligence that uses those computational resources has begun.

In AGI and ASI research, there is a concept called Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI).

AI participates in the research and development of the next generation of AI, and the superior AI created there researches and develops the next generation of AI. This is the idea that the evolution of AI itself accelerates through this cycle.

Improving coding ability alone is not enough to fully establish this cycle. Even if given instructions can be implemented perfectly, if the instructions themselves are not beneficial for research, computational resources will be wasted.

This is where the measured Research Taste becomes important. If AI evolves not only as an implementer but also as an entity responsible for experimental research decision-making, the structure of AI research and development itself may change.

In the original October 2026 paper, P-Zero Research also conducted simulations reflecting the measured upward trend in research taste in the AI Futures Model.

However, this is an extrapolation assuming a constant growth trend and is not a definitive prediction of when ASI will be reached. Furthermore, this simulation was conducted before the current measurement results of 4.9 times for GPT-6.2 Astra were announced.

Even so, it has been shown that the variable of 'research intuition' has a significant impact that cannot be ignored when considering the arrival time of superintelligence.

Here, I would also like to touch upon the limitations of TasteVal. In this benchmark, the research problems themselves are provided in advance. In other words, the ability to discover more fundamental questions—such as what should be researched in the first place—is not measured.

Additionally, the authors themselves acknowledge that the human experts used for comparison do not include the world's top-tier researchers. Since the focus is on experimental tasks where results can be verified in a relatively short period, caution is also needed regarding generalization to long-term basic research.

The ability to discover problems that humanity has not yet noticed and to open up entirely new academic fields—how far AI will acquire this remains to be seen in future research.

Today, I also wrote an article about Boaz Barak's essay 'Human empowerment in a few fake graphs,' which was highly praised by Sam Altman.

Barak presents a vision where, as AI intelligence improves, human capabilities for understanding, monitoring, and controlling AI are also expanded by AI. At the same time, he mentions the possibility that rapid intelligence gains through recursive self-improvement could outpace the expansion of human capabilities.

Immediately after that, I saw the measurement results regarding the research intuition of GPT-6.2 Astra. One side of the discussion is how humanity and rapidly evolving AI will coexist. The other is the measurement of the capabilities that could trigger that rapid evolution.

Reading these two together reveals why current AI safety research is facing such a critical juncture.

Every time a new AI model is announced, comparisons are made regarding capabilities we use daily, such as text generation, browser operation, and coding. Of course, this is an important evaluation for users.

However, if we are to consider the path to AGI and ASI, we must focus not only on what current AI can do, but also on what it can do to create the next generation of AI. From an era where humans evolve AI to an era where AI evolves AI.

These measurement results regarding the research intuition of GPT-6.2 Astra may be one important observation point indicating that this transition is underway.

P-Zero Research Official X Account (Measurement results announced on November 24, 2026) https://x.com/pzeroresearch

Introducing TasteVal — P-Zero Research https://pzeroresearch.com/work/tasteval/

Oliver Jaffe, Dane Sherburn, TasteVal: Measuring the Experimental Research Taste of AI Systems Against Human Experts (October 5, 2026) https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06824

title:

title:
Demon Slayer, Street Fighter and Shield Hero Voice Actor, Stephen Fu Celebrates 41! 🎙️🔥🎮

Stephen Fu has quickly become
title_en:
Demon Slayer, Street Fighter and Shield Hero Voice Actor, Stephen Fu Celebrates 41! 🎙️🔥🎮

Stephen Fu has quickly become a familiar voice across modern anime and gaming, bringing a striking range of heroes, villains, and fan favorites to life. His chilling performance as Douma in Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba stands alongside major game roles like Iron Fist / Lin Lie in Marvel Rivals, Jamie in Street Fighter 6, and Hwei in League of Legends.

Anime fans also know him as Naofumi Iwatani in The Rising of the Shield Hero, Weather Report in JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Stone Ocean, Sakuta Azusagawa in Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai, and Lance Crown in Mashle: Magic and Muscles. Newer roles such as Anaxa in Honkai: Star Rail, Natsuki Seba in Sakamoto Days, and Naito Mudano in Tougen Anki continue to expand an already impressive résumé.

Some of his most notable voice roles include:
• Douma — Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
• Iron Fist / Lin Lie — Marvel Rivals
• Jamie — Street Fighter 6
• Cho Sang-woo — Squid Game
• Naofumi Iwatani — The Rising of the Shield Hero
• Hwei — League of Legends
• Wise — Zenless Zone Zero
• Weather Report — JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure: Stone Ocean
• Sakuta Azusagawa — Rascal Does Not Dream of Bunny Girl Senpai
• Anaxa — Honkai: Star Rail
• Lance Crown — Mashle: Magic and Muscles
• Henry Legolant — Black Clover
• Seiji Shishikura — My Hero Academia
• Ryo Saeba — City Hunter
• Noé Archiviste — The Case Study of Vanitas
• Shinpei Ajiro — Summer Time Rendering
• Akito Yamada — My Love Story with Yamada-kun at Lv999
• Natsuki Seba — Sakamoto Days
• Naito Mudano — Tougen Anki
• Khrome Ryugu — Beyblade X

With roles spanning intense villains, laid-back leads, fighters, and emotionally complex heroes, Fu continues to make his mark across some of anime and gaming’s biggest worlds.

Happy 41st Birthday, Stephen Fu! 🎂✨

史蒂芬·傅 (Stephen Fu) 迅速成为现代动漫和游戏领域的知名人物，将一系列引人注目的英雄、反派和粉丝最爱的角色带入生活。他在《鬼灭之刃》中饰演 Douma 的令人毛骨悚然的表演，与《漫威对手》中的铁拳 / 林烈、《街头霸王 6》中的 Jamie 以及《英雄联盟》中的 Hwei 等主要游戏角色齐名。

动漫迷们还知道他在《盾之勇者成名录》中扮演岩谷尚文、在《JoJo的奇妙冒险：石之海》中扮演天气预报、在《青春猪头少年不会梦到兔女郎学姐》中的梓川咲太以及在《魔法与肌肉》中扮演兰斯·克朗。新角色，如《崩坏：星轨》中的阿那克萨、《坂本时代》中的濑叶夏希以及《桃源 Anki》中的内藤·穆达诺，继续扩大本已令人印象深刻的履历。

他的一些最著名的配音角色包括：
• Douma — 鬼灭之刃：Kimetsu no Yaiba
• 铁拳 / 林烈 — Marvel Rivals
• 杰米 — 街头霸王 6
• Cho Sang-woo — 鱿鱼游戏
• 岩谷尚文 — 《盾之勇者成名录》

• 梓川咲太 — 青春猪头少年不会梦到兔女郎学姐
• Anaxa — 崩坏：星轨
• Lance Crown — Mashle：魔法与肌肉
• 亨利·莱戈兰特——《黑色四叶草》
• 狮子仓精二 — 我的英雄学院
• Ryo Saeba — 城市猎人
• Noé Archiviste — Vanitas 案例研究
• Shinpei Ajiro — 夏季渲染
• Akito Yamada — 我与山田君的爱情故事 Lv999
• 濑场夏希 — 坂本时代
• 内藤·穆达诺 — Tougen Anki
• Khrome Ryugu — Beyblade X

傅的角色涵盖激烈的反派、悠闲的主角、战士和情感复杂的英雄，他继续在动漫和游戏的一些最大的世界中留下自己的印记。

傅士芬 41 岁生日快乐！ 🎂✨

title: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance
title_en: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance
title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra引领机器人控制基准突破
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra has demonstrated performance 5x above the previous two-year trend on robotic control benchmarks. Given the accelerated pace of benchmark saturation, AI models are on track to handle nearly all tracked robotic control tasks by the end of 2027.
summary_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra在机器人控制基准测试中表现卓越，预计2027年将覆盖大部分任务。
article_content:
According to Greg Brockman citing Playground on X, GPT-6.2 Astra scores sit nearly 5x above the past two years’ trend on robot-control benchmarks, with tasks on track to saturate by 2027.

On November 24 2026 Greg Brockman posted that robotics control is undergoing a renaissance driven by rapid gains in AI model performance.

According to the post Playground GPT-6.2 Astra sits nearly five times above the exponential trend of the prior two years on robot-control benchmarks while benchmarks themselves are saturating roughly ten times faster than the year before. If the pace observed since September continues top policies could saturate nearly every tracked task by the end of 2027.

full_text_en: Robotics control is undergoing a renaissance

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: OpenAI旗下的GPT-6.2 Astra在机器人控制基准测试中表现出超越过往两年趋势5倍的性能增长。随着基准测试迭代速度的加快，若当前增长态势延续，预计到2027年底，AI模型将实现对主流机器人控制任务的全面饱和覆盖。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra has demonstrated performance 5x above the previous two-year trend on robotic control benchmarks. Given the accelerated pace of benchmark saturation, AI models are on track to handle nearly all tracked robotic control tasks by the end of 2027.

summary_zh: 商汤科技发布SenseNova U1.6多模态模型，通过原生集成ComfyUI实现图像生成的自我文本校正与4K高保真渲染能力。
summary_en: SenseTime has launched SenseNova U1.6, based on the Neo-unify architecture, featuring enhanced natural language instruction parsing and visual structure mapping. The model integrates natively with ComfyUI, enabling self-correction of generated image text and delivering improved 4K rendering fidelity.

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 商汤科技正式推出SenseNova U1.6模型，该版本基于Neo-unify架构，核心突破在于增强了模型对复杂自然语言指令的解析与视觉结构映射能力。该模型通过ComfyUI工作流实现了图像生成过程中的文本自检与纠错功能，显著提升了密集文本渲染的准确度及4K画质表现。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: SenseTime has launched SenseNova U1.6, based on the Neo-unify architecture, featuring enhanced natural language instruction parsing and visual structure mapping. The model integrates natively with ComfyUI, enabling self-correction of generated image text and delivering improved 4K rendering fidelity.

elements_zh.where: ComfyUI生态系统
elements_zh.what: 发布SenseNova U1.6模型，引入原生自我校正机制与4K分辨率优化
elements_zh.why: 解决图像生成中文字拼写错误及复杂指令遵循能力不足的行业痛点

elements_en.what: Released SenseNova U1.6 with native self-correction and 4K optimization
elements_en.why: Addressing industry-wide challenges in text rendering accuracy and complex prompt adherence

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 模型将“自我修正”机制前置到推理环节，标志着多模态生成正从“概率性出图”向“确定性控制”演进。此举通过ComfyUI原生插件化策略，极大降低了开发者实现高精度复杂视觉任务的工程门槛，将对现有的Midjourney等闭源方案形成高效的生产力替代竞争。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Moving the 'self-correction' mechanism into the inference loop signifies a shift from probabilistic generation to deterministic control in multimodal AI. By leveraging native ComfyUI integration, SenseTime lowers the engineering barrier for complex visual tasks, challenging incumbent closed-source solutions with superior production utility.

ai_analysis.takeaway_zh: ERNIE系列通过接入vLLM插件，实质上是百度在开源推理基础设施层面的生态卡位，旨在降低开发者在其MoE模型上的落地门槛。此举不仅是对抗同类长上下文模型竞争的差异化策略，更是通过与主流推理框架的深度绑定，加速其模型在私有化部署市场的份额渗透。
ai_analysis.takeaway_en: By integrating with the vLLM plugin, Baidu is strategically securing its position within the open-source inference ecosystem to lower barriers for MoE model deployment. This move serves as a competitive play against other long-context models, aiming to accelerate market penetration in private deployment by aligning with standardized inference infrastructures.

title:
He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about
title_en:
He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about a guy who printed a contract and used a mechanical pencil.

Rather than skim it for 12 seconds, whisper “good for him,” and move on with my evening, I did something radical.

I didn’t print your post on a Wi-Fi laser printer like some kind of Silicon Valley soft-hands.

I transcribed every single one of your 902 words by hand onto unbleached calfskin vellum using a goose quill I cured in my own garage, sharpened it with a dull pocketknife until my thumb bled, and spent four and a half hours marking up the margins in homemade iron-gall ink.

I finished writing down my thoughts in the margins, set down my quill, stared silently at a brass lamp, and reflected on what just happened.

I felt deeply satisfied, wildly embarrassed, mildly dehydrated, and somehow taller all at once.

I couldn’t remember the last time I had used my brain for an end-to-end process without relying on an industrial convenience like a mechanical pencil or Hewlett-Packard toner. I felt total command over your post. I felt crystalline clarity about what I understood, what I didn’t understand, and why a grown man felt moved to alert the entire timeline that he had read a PDF with a pencil. And I was left with unshakable conviction in my POV.

Moreover, I felt the high of “ultra-clean” dopamine.

Not the factory-farmed, seed-oil dopamine you get from pressing a plastic thumb-clicker on a 0.7mm Pentel like a lab rat tapping a lever for pellets. Not the lukewarm, ultra-processed dopamine of reading a contract printed out on bleached 20-pound copy paper that a machine collated for you without even asking you to set the movable type.

No. I’m talking about single-origin, cold-pressed, pasture-raised dopamine. The kind of raw, unadulterated neurochemical high our ancestors felt when they sat down at a mahogany desk, read an actual contract from page one to the signature block, and didn’t immediately open LinkedIn to announce that they had survived the ordeal.

Then I felt embarrassed.

How long had I been depriving myself of turning basic adult errands into sweeping civilizational manifestos?

Just yesterday, I made two slices of sourdough toast without once asking Claude to “review this loaf, break down the crumb structure, and give me feedback as if you’re my baker.” I stood there in front of the toaster like a pioneer on the Oregon Trail, watched the heating coils glow orange, buttered the bread manually, and ate it. And what did I do afterward? Nothing. I just rinsed my plate and went to work. Not a single 1,000-word reflection on the erosion of culinary agency. Not one mention of Socrates. Not one bulleted list of ways to reclaim the sacred space between bread and butter.

I was disgusted with myself.

And then I got curious.

In fact, I got so curious that I had to sit down, because curiosity at this altitude can make a man lightheaded.

Why is it that every time somebody in tech rediscovers an office supply from 1987, he feels spiritually compelled to summon Daniel Kahneman, Socrates, and Viktor Frankl like the Avengers? And what can we do to make sure we don’t surrender our last remaining shred of self-awareness to the Thought Leadership Industrial Complex?

The answer lies in what Daniel Kahneman called System 1 and System 2 thinking, and more importantly, in the three higher systems that Kahneman was too polite to put in the book.

Everyone on the internet loves citing System 1 and System 2, mostly because Thinking, Fast and Slow is the single most-referenced book among people who read a four-page summary of it in 2016 and have been dining out on the phrase “lazy controller” ever since.

System 1 is fast, automatic, and gut-driven thought. It’s what fires when a 42-page commercial agreement lands in your inbox on a Thursday afternoon and your brain immediately says, “I am not reading all of this, I should probably pay an actual lawyer instead of asking a chatbot to roleplay as one.”

System 2 is deliberate, analytical, effortful, and conscious. It’s what fires when you ignore System 1, print the 42-page agreement yourself, grab a mechanical pencil, write “check indemnity??” and “what does mutatis mutandis mean” in the margins for 90 minutes, and walk away from your desk feeling like John Marshall presiding over Marbury v. Madison.

But stopping at System 2 is rookie-level cognition. If you really want to diagnose what is happening to the human mind in 2026, you have to go deeper:

System 3 is performing System 2 in public so strangers know you still have a prefrontal cortex. You didn’t merely read the contract. You observed yourself reading the contract from a cinematic third-person camera angle, felt a single noble tear roll down your cheek, and started mentally workshopping the opening hook somewhere around Section 7.2(b).

System 4 is taking a completely normal Tuesday afternoon task (reading a document before you sign it) and laundering it through one ancient Greek philosopher, three cognitive psychologists, a misattributed quote, ten repetitive bullet points, and a closing comparison to the sun until a routine administrative chore sounds like the drafting of the Magna Carta.

System 5 is reading someone else’s System 4 post and concluding that the only proportionate moral response is to construct an even longer, even more grandiose System 4 post, thereby testing the structural load limits of the X Premium character counter and everybody’s patience simultaneously.

Technology has been hijacking effortful thinking for far longer than 370 BC. Frankly, starting the timeline with Socrates is System 1 history.

Roughly a million years ago: Fire hijacked raw-meat mastication as a gastrointestinal System 2 exercise. Early hominids no longer had to chew elk cartilage for four uninterrupted hours just to extract 300 calories. Immediate metabolic offloading. Everything went downhill from there.

3200 BC: Sumerian cuneiform hijacked remembering how many goats your brother-in-law owed you from the spring harvest. Within two generations, nobody could keep track of a single goat in their head. Pure cognitive atrophy.

1440 AD: Gutenberg’s printing press hijacked the deeply satisfying, hard-fought labor of being a medieval monk squinting in an unheated stone scriptorium for eleven years to hand-copy one manuscript by tallow candle. Did anyone pause to ask what the printing press was doing to the monks’ taste?

1784: Bifocals hijacked squinting as an ocular System 2 exercise.

1822: John Isaac Hawkins and Sampson Mordan secured British Patent No. 4742 for the first mechanical pencil, explicitly designed in the words of the patent itself for “rendering the frequent cutting or mending of the points or nibs unnecessary.”

Stop and sit with that for a moment.

The very mechanical pencil you held aloft yesterday as your Excalibur against Silicon Valley is itself a 204-year-old machine engineered to offload the noble, character-building friction of whittling cedarwood with a blade and blowing graphite dust off your thumb. You didn’t reject shortcuts. You just picked a Victorian shortcut and called it enlightenment.

1959: The Xerox 914 photocopier hijacked retyping contracts on carbon paper.

1983: Microsoft Word hijacked Wite-Out and the healthy, adrenaline-soaked terror of making a typo on page 14 of a 15-page lease.

Calculators hijacked long division.
GPS hijacked arguing with your spouse over a folded Rand McNally road atlas on the center console while missing the exit for Savannah.
Google hijacked sitting at a bar for three hours insisting to your friends that Kevin Costner was in Air Force One when it was actually Harrison Ford, the kind of hard-fought, unadulterated barstool conviction that used to build real character.

And this.

2. Accountability
3. Relationships
4. Judgement

5. Printing a 30-page PDF so you can carry it around the house looking burdened and important.

7. Buying a $65 brass mechanical pencil from a specialty stationery shop in Kyoto so your margin notes have better mouthfeel.
8. Calling regular job satisfaction “clean dopamine” because saying “I felt good about finishing my work” doesn’t sound like a Huberman episode.
9. Assuming that because you used to outsource your thinking to Claude, the rest of Western civilization forgot how to read a document.

AI is a very fast autocomplete machine wired into a warehouse of GPUs that helps people turn a three-sentence email into a keynote about human destiny.

Yes, it may put a tutor in every child’s hands.

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。
author: Coastal Country Club
summary_zh:
没有像硅谷的软手那样使用 Wi-Fi 激光打印机打印你的文章。

我用在自家车库里腌制的鹅毛笔，将你的 902 个单词中的每一个字都手写在未漂白的小牛皮牛皮纸上，用钝的小刀将其削尖，直到我的拇指流血，并花了四个半小时用自制的铁胆墨水标记边缘。

我在页边写完自己的想法，放下羽毛笔，默默地盯着一盏铜灯，思考着刚刚发生的事情。

我感到深深的满足、极度的尴尬、轻微的脱水，但不知何故突然长高了。

我不记得上次我在不依赖自动铅笔或惠普碳粉等工业便利设施的情况下使用大脑进行端到端流程是什么时候了。我对你的帖子感到完全掌控。我对自己理解的内容、不理解的内容感到非常清晰，也明白了为什么一个成年人会因为提醒整个时间线他用铅笔阅读了一份 PDF 而感到感动。我对自己的观点有着不可动摇的信念。

此外，我还感受到了“超洁净”多巴胺的快感。

不是工厂化养殖的种子油多巴胺，是通过在 0.7 毫米 Pentel 上按下塑料拇指点击器而获得的，就像实验室老鼠敲击颗粒杠杆一样。阅读打印在漂白的 20 磅复印纸上的合同时，机器会帮你校对，甚至不需要你设置活字印刷，这不是那种不冷不热、经过过度处理的多巴胺。

不，我说的是单一来源、冷榨、牧场饲养的多巴胺。当我们的祖先坐在桃花心木办公桌前，从第一页读到签名栏，阅读一份真实的合同，并且没有立即打开 LinkedIn 宣布他们已经从这场磨难中幸存下来时，他们感受到了那种原始的、纯粹的神经化学物质的兴奋。

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。

full_text_zh:
@FutureJurvetson @elonmusk @kimmonismus 背景：
“在过去 20 年的大部分时间里，我一直在尝试训练模型进行视频预测，但在前 15 年基本上失败了。直到我意识到必须放弃生成模型并使用联合嵌入预测架构 (JEPA)”

“过去几年，JEPA 和世界模型开始发挥作用。主要应用是物理世界、机器人和工业过程控制。Meta 对这些东西不是特别感兴趣”

但我的项目始终得到扎克、博兹、施雷普和克里斯·考克斯的支持。

确实，作为首席人工智能科学家，我虽然是高级副总裁级别，但却是一名 IC。公司最好的工作！

我从未攻读过法学硕士，这也是事实。我非常支持 FAIR 的 LLM 项目（例如后来成为 Llama 的项目），并在说服 Mark 围绕 Llama 创建人工智能优先产品部门方面发挥了作用，并推动开源 Llama-2。但我从来没有参与过技术层面的工作。

title: GPT-6.2 Astra is a step function on robotics:
title_en: GPT-6.2 Astra is a step function on robotics:
title_zh: GPT-6.2 Astra 是机器人技术的阶跃函数：
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_zh:
OpenAI 的最新模型在 Artificial Analysis 的物理机器人基准测试中得分为 79 分，击败了其更便宜的同类产品 Claude Fable 5.2

OpenAI 的 GPT-6.2 Astra 在 AA-Robotics v0.1 上获得第一名，该基准测试语言模型是否可以操作真正的机器人手臂。 Astra 的平均得分为 79
article_content:
OpenAI's newest model scored 79 on Artificial Analysis's physical robotics benchmark, edging out its cheaper sibling and Claude Fable 5.2

OpenAI’s GPT-6.2 Astra has claimed first place on AA-Robotics v0.1, a benchmark that tests whether language models can operate a real robot arm. Astra posted an average score of 79 out of 100, the highest in the evaluation.

It also did it with less fuss than anyone else. Astra used the fewest arm commands of any model tested, which suggests it is getting better at planning before it starts moving.

AA-Robotics v0.1 comes from Artificial Analysis, which launched the benchmark on October 14, 2026. It puts frontier language models in charge of a 6-axis Hiwonder NexArm robot arm.

The models do not control the arm by feel. They act as coding agents, writing instructions that the hardware then carries out.

The tasks include pouring drinks and stacking blocks. Both demand spatial awareness and problem-solving, two areas where text-trained models have historically been shaky.

Astra finished six of the eight tasks in the evaluation. Its 79 average put it just ahead of GPT-6.2 Sol, OpenAI’s more affordable variant, which scored 78. Claude Fable 5.2 came in at 75.

Astra issued 668 arm commands in total across its six completed tasks. On the box-cleanup task alone, it needed only 92 commands. That figure is approximately 75% fewer than Claude Fable 5.2 required.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Every command sent to a physical arm is a chance for something to go wrong. Fewer commands generally means less trial and error, less wasted motion, and less wear on hardware.

The models still take about 30 minutes per task. A human handles comparable tasks in around 20 seconds.

Cost is another constraint. Running the models on these tasks costs between $2 and $16 per task, depending on the model and the job.

OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra on November 17, 2026. It shipped alongside GPT-6.2 Sol, positioned as the lower-cost option.

Astra’s API pricing is approximately 20% lower than its predecessor’s.

The robotics result lands about a month after Artificial Analysis introduced the benchmark. That timing means Astra arrived to a leaderboard that was still freshly painted, with Claude Fable 5.2 among the models already evaluated.

The tight finish between Astra and Sol also deserves attention. If the cheaper model lands within one point of the flagship on physical tasks, developers building robotics prototypes may reasonably ask whether the premium tier is worth it.

The gaps that remain are equally instructive. A 30-minute task time against a 20-second human baseline shows how far general-purpose models are from practical deployment. Per-task costs of $2 to $16 add another hurdle for any business doing the math on automation.

The label on the benchmark matters too. This is version 0.1.

Disclosure: This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. For more information on how we create and review content, see our Editorial Policy.

title: SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.
title_en:
SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.

Now, SBI is India's biggest bank. Its balance sheet crossed ₹66 lakh crore this year. Almost every Indian family has some link to it, a salary account, a home loan, a pension.

In October, SBI put out an ad for six AI and tech roles. There is one opening for "General Manager and Chief AI Officer".

The pay is up to ₹1.6 crore a year. SBI says it depends on experience, current pay and posting.

The other five roles pay well too. Three Deputy General Managers get up to ₹1.2 crore each. Two AI architects get up to ₹90 lakh each.

Now SBI's own chairman, CS Setty drew ₹63.87 lakh in FY25. So the AI chief can earn about 2.5 times the person who runs the bank.

Yet, private banks are a different world. 

HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan was paid ₹12.08 crore in FY25. PSU bank CEOs earn only about 5 to 7% of what private bank CEOs earn.

But SBI able to pay its AI chief more than its chairman, because the role is a contract job. It is a three year term, which SBI can extend by two more years.

Basically, it is the workaround. An AI leader at this level won't come at this budget. So SBI is working around it.

As per the ad, the person will set up control rooms for AI and data products with the business teams. They will track how live AI models perform and what risks they carry. 

They will also run a separate team whose job is to check models independently. They will also train staff to use these tools. The role also covers an enterprise AI platform for generative AI and AI agents.

They need at least 15 years in banking, financial services or IT. And at least 3 years in a senior leadership role in AI, analytics, model oversight or governance.

So a brilliant engineer who built great models alone, but never ran a team, can't apply for this.

Honestly, a three year term is very short for building an AI platform inside a bank this size. SBI should use the two year extension while they build a second line of leaders under the CAIO from day one.

Obviously, a chairman earning less than half of what a new hire under him can earn is not a healthy setup. 

The Finance Ministry should let PSU banks pay market rates for specialist roles through a clear policy, instead of a contract workaround every time.

And if you are a senior data or analytics person who wants a role like this in five years, it rewards people who have led teams, owned model risk and worked with business heads. 

Pure technical depth won't be enough.

full_text_zh:
SBI 为首席人工智能官提供的 1.6 亿卢比的报价很棒，但这也表明 PSU 银行对技术人才的薪酬是多么的破碎。

现在，SBI 是印度最大的银行。今年其资产负债表超过 660 亿卢比。几乎每个印度家庭都与它有某种联系，工资账户、住房贷款、养老金。

10 月，SBI 发布了一则招聘 6 个人工智能和技术职位的广告。有一个“总经理兼首席人工智能官”的职位空缺。

年薪高达 1600 万卢比。 SBI 表示，这取决于经验、当前薪酬和职位。

其他五个角色的报酬也不错。三名副总经理每人的薪酬最高可达 12 万卢比。两名人工智能架构师每人可获得高达 900 万卢比的奖金。

CS Setty 现任 SBI 董事长，2025 财年收入达 638.7 万卢比。因此，人工智能主管的收入大约是银行经营者的 2.5 倍。

然而，私人银行却是一个不同的世界。

HDFC 银行首席执行官 Sashidhar Jagdishan 在 2025 财年的薪酬为 1.208 亿卢比。 PSU 银行首席执行官的收入仅为私人银行首席执行官的 5% 至 7% 左右。

但 SBI 能够向 AI 主管支付比董事长更高的薪酬，因为该职位是合同制工作。任期三年，SBI 可以再延长两年。

基本上，这是解决方法。这个级别的人工智能领导者不会有这样的预算。因此，SBI 正在解决这个问题。

根据广告，此人将与业务团队一起建立人工智能和数据产品的控制室。他们将跟踪实时人工智能模型的表现以及它们带来的风险。

他们还将管理一个单独的团队，其工作是独立检查模型。他们还将培训员工使用这些工具。该角色还涵盖用于生成人工智能和人工智能代理的企业人工智能平台。

他们需要在银行、金融服务或 IT 行业工作至少 15 年。并在人工智能、分析、模型监督或治理领域担任高级领导职务至少 3 年。

因此，一位才华横溢的工程师独自构建了出色的模型，但从未管理过团队，因此无法申请此职位。

老实说，对于在这种规模的银行内部构建人工智能平台来说，三年的期限非常短。 SBI 应该利用两年的延期，从第一天起就在 CAIO 下建立第二线领导人。

显然，董事长的收入还不到他手下新员工收入的一半，这并不是一个健康的设置。

财政部应该通过明确的政策，让事业单位银行为专家角色支付市场利率，而不是每次都通过合同解决办法。

如果你是一名高级数据或分析人员，希望在五年内担任这样的职位，那么它会奖励那些领导团队、承担模型风险并与业务主管合作的人。

纯粹的技术深度是不够的。

title_en:
@peter_godman @john__allard There is a difference between
- the capital of France is Düsseldorf <eos>
- the capital of France is Düsseldorf, oh wait I misspoke, it's Paris <eos>
The first one is an unrecoverable mistake.
The second one is correct.
The tree of <eos>-terminated sequences is .... a tree.
Errors are unrecoverable.

第二个是正确的。
以 <eos> 结尾的序列

title_en:
@TheSadMan25 @RajeswarSai I did not make a bet against LLMs.
I supported research on LLMs at FAIR.
Meta made a big bet on LLMs and dialog systems, first as a research project since 2014, then as a product line since 2023 with Llama 2, 3, and 4.
I was never involved in the product effort.
I was not involved in management since 2018, I was an IC, preferring to concentrate on research in SSL and world models.
Llama-4 was a disappointment, largely because time pressure made the team overly conservative. 
My new company is focusing on world models and doing fine, thank you very much.
full_text_en:
@TheSadMan25 @RajeswarSai I did not make a bet against LLMs.
I supported research on LLMs at FAIR.
Meta made a big bet on LLMs and dialog systems, first as a research project since 2014, then as a product line since 2023 with Llama 2, 3, and 4.
I was never involved in the product effort.
I was not involved in management since 2018, I was an IC, preferring to concentrate on research in SSL and world models.
Llama-4 was a disappointment, largely because time pressure made the team overly conservative. 
My new company is focusing on world models and doing fine, thank you very much.
full_text_zh:
@TheSadMan25 @RajeswarSai 我没有打赌法学硕士。
我支持 FAIR 的法学硕士研究。
Meta 在法学硕士和对话系统上下了很大的赌注，首先从 2014 年开始作为一个研究项目，然后从 2023 年开始作为 Llama 2、3 和 4 的产品线。
我从未参与过产品工作。
我从2018年开始就没有参与管理，我是一名IC，更喜欢专注于SSL和世界模型的研究。
Llama-4 令人失望，主要是因为时间压力使团队过于保守。
我的新公司专注于世界模特并且做得很好，非常感谢。

title_en: Google AI ultra also comes with $100/mo in Google cloud credits, which can be used for straight up API inference If the models keep getting this good it’s gonna be another Amazon prime situation where it just makes sense
title_zh: 谷歌订阅计划绑定云端API额度策略
author: @wesbos
summary_en: Google is providing AI Premium subscribers with $100 in monthly Google Cloud API credits, effectively integrating consumer subscription services with developer infrastructure. This strategy lowers the barrier to entry for API-based inference and aims to cultivate long-term platform stickiness through ecosystem locking.
summary_zh: 谷歌通过为AI Premium用户提供每月100美元的云端API调用额度，加速其开发生态与消费级订阅的深度整合。

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 谷歌正在采取类似亚马逊Prime的生态捆绑逻辑，通过订阅制将开发者与云端推理成本直接挂钩，意在抵消模型性能提升带来的高算力开销。此举本质上是对冲API调用量流失的防御性策略，旨在通过预付消费模式锁定模型推理的长期存量市场。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Google is employing an Amazon Prime-style bundling strategy, linking subscription fees directly to cloud inference costs to offset the growing compute intensity of high-performance models. This effectively secures long-term market share for inference by shifting from usage-based billing to recurring, prepay-based ecosystem capture.

title:
TOTALLY  COOKED

Brooke is a perfect case study in what happens when climate alarmism fully liquefies a person’s capacit
title_en:
TOTALLY  COOKED

Brooke is a perfect case study in what happens when climate alarmism fully liquefies a person’s capacity for rational thought. 

She has, quite literally, lost the ability to process basic data and has instead retreated into a cult that requires constant existential dread as proof of membership.

The data is clear  -  the numbers are not ambiguous. 

We have never been safer from climate-related disasters at any point in human history. The chance of dying from one is more than 98% lower than it was a century ago. 

Every major indicator shows the opposite of the apocalypse she has been trained to fear: sustained global greening, declining disaster mortality, and a climate that has been slowly recovering from the Little Ice Age.

We should be rejoicing. 

None of this is secret. It is simply inconvenient to the business model of the climate grifters and the media outlets (ABC and the rest of the usual suspects) that amplify them. 

Brooke has been so thoroughly propagandized that she is now “genuinely afraid for her life” over a risk that has collapsed by an order of magnitude. 

That is not awareness. That is the intellectual equivalent of still believing in monsters under the bed long after the lights have been turned on and the data presented.

By choosing to remain in that state, she is no longer merely harming herself. 

For one can live a full, productive life while they are "genuinely afraid for their lives".

Further, she is harming other impressionable people who might be influenced by her emotional fact-free nonsense and fall into the same self-inflicted neurosis.

The only remaining hope is that some residual capacity for independent thought still exists and that Brooke eventually develops the curiosity—or at least the self-respect—actually read the Evidenve and leave the cult.

full_text_zh:
完全煮熟

布鲁克是一个完美的案例，研究了当气候危言耸听完全削弱一个人的理性思考能力时会发生什么。

毫不夸张地说，她已经失去了处理基本数据的能力，而是退回到一个需要持续存在的恐惧作为其成员身份的证明的邪教中。

数据很清楚——数字并不含糊。

在人类历史上的任何时候，我们从未如此安全地免受与气候相关的灾难的影响。与一个世纪前相比，死于这种疾病的几率降低了 98% 以上。

每一项主要指标都显示出与她所害怕的世界末日相反的一面：全球持续绿化、灾害死亡率下降，以及从小冰河时代缓慢恢复的气候。

我们应该庆幸。

这些都不是秘密。这对于气候欺诈者和放大他们的媒体机构（美国广播公司和其他通常的嫌疑人）的商业模式来说根本不方便。

布鲁克受到了如此彻底的宣传，以至于她现在“真正担心自己的生命安全”，因为风险已经下降了一个数量级。

那不是意识。这相当于在灯打开、数据呈现很久之后仍然相信床底下有怪物。

通过选择保持这种状态，她不再只是在伤害自己。

因为当一个人“真正担心自己的生命安全”时，他们仍然可以过上充实、富有成效的生活。

此外，她正在伤害其他易受影响的人，这些人可能会受到她情感上与事实无关的胡言乱语的影响，并陷入同样的​​自我造成的神经症。

唯一剩下的希望是，一些独立思考的残余能力仍然存在，布鲁克最终会产生好奇心——或者至少是自尊——真正阅读《证据》并离开邪教。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 初创公司Thinky Machines发布Inkling 2 Mini模型，该模型总参数量为26.4B，在Agent Arena基准测试中以996分跃居榜单第18位，位列美国开源模型第3名。相比其594B参数量的Small版本，该小型化模型在保持高智能体任务处理能力的同时，显著降低了推理算力门槛。

elements_zh.where: Agent Arena评估榜单
elements_zh.what: 发布参数量26.4B的Inkling 2 Mini模型
elements_zh.why: 旨在通过参数剪枝实现高效的智能体任务推理

elements_en.what: Released 26.4B Inkling 2 Mini model
elements_en.why: To achieve efficient agentic reasoning through parameter optimization

ai_analysis.insight_zh: Inkling 2 Mini的成功验证了智能体专用模型（Agentic Models）在参数缩减后仍能保持强劲逻辑表现的技术路径。在当前大模型向端侧部署迁移的趋势下，此类模型通过牺牲非必要参数换取高推理效率，将直接冲击中小型垂直AI应用的市场竞争格局。
ai_analysis.insight_en: The success of Inkling 2 Mini validates the technical trajectory of agent-specific models that maintain strong reasoning despite smaller parameter counts. As LLMs shift towards edge deployment, such models, which exchange redundant parameters for high inference efficiency, will disrupt the market for mid-to-small vertical AI applications.

title: Attackers use AI agent swarms to exploit vulnerabilities in hours. Patches take weeks. Today, Cisco & OpenAI launch Shirudo, an open-source platform that uses eBPF to shield running Linux systems at machine speed without disruptions. Read more: https://t.c
title_en: Attackers use AI agent swarms to exploit vulnerabilities in hours. Patches take weeks. Today, Cisco & OpenAI launch Shirudo, an open-source platform that uses eBPF to shield running Linux systems at machine speed without disruptions. Read more: https://t.c
title_zh: 思科与OpenAI发布开源平台Shirudo
author: @CiscoSecure
summary_en: Cisco and OpenAI have launched Shirudo, an open-source security platform utilizing eBPF technology. title: GPT-6.2 has an incredible understanding of the 3D world:
title_en: GPT-6.2 has an incredible understanding of the 3D world:
title_zh: OpenAI发布GPT-6.2模型系列，强化三维仿真与工程自动化
author: Greg Brockman
author_role: OpenAI 总裁兼联合创始人
summary_en: OpenAI released the GPT-6.2 model series, featuring the Astra model which achieved a leading 1,318 Elo score on the AA-3D benchmark. By integrating multimodal inputs with external software control, Astra enables end-to-end engineering workflows ranging from sketches to CAD modeling and mechanical simulation.
summary_zh: OpenAI于2026年11月17日推出GPT-6.2系列，包括专业级Astra与轻量级Sol模型，旨在通过多模态感知与工具调用实现三维世界建模与工程自动化。
article_content:
OpenAI says its newest model family, GPT-6.2, can understand and simulate three-dimensional worlds. It can also help users create them.

The release landed on November 17, 2026, and it came as a pair. GPT-6.2 Astra is the heavy-duty option, aimed at professional and scientific work. GPT-6.2 Sol is the lighter, everyday sibling.

Astra is the one carrying the 3D headline. It posted a score of 1,318 Elo on AA-3D, an independent benchmark for three-dimensional tasks. That put it in the top spot.

The closest rival on AA-3D was Claude Fable 5.2, at 1,271 Elo. That is a 47-point gap at the top of the table.

The more concrete pitch is what Astra can actually produce. OpenAI says it can take a plain text prompt and turn it into a fully interactive 3D scene. Demonstrations included a pendulum clock with simulated mechanics and simulations of car dynamics.

The most telling demo was a complete engineering workflow. Astra reportedly went from a rough sketch to CAD parts, then to a Python solver that calculated motion. It finished with a Blender scene, complete with instructions.

That workflow depends on two features shared by both Astra and Sol. First, they are multimodal, meaning they accept images alongside text. A user can hand over a sketch instead of describing it in a paragraph.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Second, both models can use external tools. They can run code and control software, including CAD programs and Blender. Chaining those abilities together is what makes multistep simulation pipelines possible.

Astra’s specific goal is to lower the cost of running these multistep tasks for engineering and scientific users. Sol, meanwhile, targets ordinary tasks and brings notable efficiency gains compared with earlier models.

One caveat stands out. Initial reports did not mention physical 3D printing or any real-world testing of the designs Astra produced.

The company has framed GPT-6.2 as a sizable improvement in cost efficiency per task over its earlier models.

The split into Astra and Sol also reflects a familiar strategy. One model handles the expensive, demanding jobs. The other covers routine work at lower cost, where most daily usage tends to happen.

The research behind this release points to manufacturing, automotive, and architecture as sectors that could feel the effects.

Astra’s lead over Claude Fable 5.2 on AA-3D is meaningful but not enormous. In a market where model releases arrive in rapid succession, a 47-point margin can shrink quickly.

GPT-6.2 works by operating CAD and 3D tools, not replacing them. For now, that makes AI a new kind of power user rather than a direct competitor.

Disclosure: This article was edited by Diego Almada Lopez. For more information on how we create and review content, see our Editorial Policy.

title:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it pro
title_en:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it properly:

• Write down how your best person does it today
• Write the spec before the agent writes any code
• If you can write the rule down, make it code instead of an LLM call
• Use the team's own wrong answers from last quarter as the test set
• Score the agent on that test set before anyone relies on it
• Run it in your own cloud tenant so the data stays put
• Give it read access first and write access later
• Make a person approve anything that moves money, emails a customer or deletes data
• Cap every run on time and cost
• Log every model call, tool call and decision
• Track cost per finished task
• Run it alongside the people doing the job for a few weeks and compare
• Turn every complaint into a new test case
• Block changes when the test score drops
• Keep the old process alive until the numbers hold
• Tell the team what it's for before it ships
• Give it one month, then decide

Say the workflow is invoice coding and your team caught 40 wrong codes last quarter. Those 40 are your test set. If the agent gets 37 right, the 3 it misses usually show you a rule nobody wrote down. That's worth finding even if you never ship the agent.

• 写下你最好的人今天是如何做的

full_text_en:
Do yourself a favor!

Pick one painful, boring workflow in your company and build an agent that fixes it. Then do it properly:

• Write down how your best person does it today
• Write the spec before the agent writes any code
• If you can write the rule down, make it code instead of an LLM call
• Use the team's own wrong answers from last quarter as the test set
• Score the agent on that test set before anyone relies on it
• Run it in your own cloud tenant so the data stays put
• Give it read access first and write access later
• Make a person approve anything that moves money, emails a customer or deletes data
• Cap every run on time and cost
• Log every model call, tool call and decision
• Track cost per finished task
• Run it alongside the people doing the job for a few weeks and compare
• Turn every complaint into a new test case
• Block changes when the test score drops
• Keep the old process alive until the numbers hold
• Tell the team what it's for before it ships
• Give it one month, then decide

Say the workflow is invoice coding and your team caught 40 wrong codes last quarter. Those 40 are your test set. If the agent gets 37 right, the 3 it misses usually show you a rule nobody wrote down. That's worth finding even if you never ship the agent.

Most of what I've learned from 40 AI agents in production fits on this list.

Do the first one end to end, and the second goes a lot faster because the test set, the logging and the approvals already exist.

帮自己一个忙！

• 写下你最好的人今天是如何做的
• 在代理编写任何代码之前编写规范
• 如果您可以写下规则，请将其编码而不是LLM调用
• 使用团队自己上季度的错误答案作为测试集
• 在任何人依赖该测试集之前对代理进行评分
• 在您自己的云租户中运行它，以便数据保持不变
• 首先授予其读取权限，然后授予写入权限
• 让某人批准任何转移资金、向客户发送电子邮件或删除数据的行为
• 限制每次运行的时间和成本
• 记录每个模型调用、工具调用和决策
• 跟踪每个已完成任务的成本
• 与从事这项工作的人员一起运行几周并进行比较
• 将每一个投诉转化为一个新的测试用例
• 当测试分数下降时阻止更改
• 保持旧进程处于活动状态，直到数字保持不变
• 在发货前告诉团队它的用途
• 给它一个月的时间，然后再决定

Gavin's point is that there are lots of companies generating lots of revenue with open source models, and that those substantial figures are not counted in the "Anthropic Plus OpenAI Plus Grok/Gemini ARR" calculations many investors use to estimate ROI of AI CapEx. 

He says second derivative of AI CapEx has "probably peaked" and that "the market is very focused on the second derivative..." but he thinks this will be "a semiconductor cycle much longer than what's in recent memory," and that the AI build-out "may end up being more like the railroads," which were a big chunk of American GDP for ~60 years.

Recorded at @TomorrowXSummit, November 18th, after Nvidia earnings and before Jensen's reinstatement today.

title: Inkling 2 Mini by Thinking Machines. Looped transformer, 26.4B params, runs on ~20GB memory, and surprisingly strong coding benchmarks. 77.9% on SWE-bench Pro Hard is impressive for a model this size. https://t.co/feBM5VqthQ
title_en: Inkling 2 Mini by Thinking Machines. Looped transformer, 26.4B params, runs on ~20GB memory, and surprisingly strong coding benchmarks. 77.9% on SWE-bench Pro Hard is impressive for a model this size. https://t.co/feBM5VqthQ
title_zh: Thinking Machines 的 Inkling 2 Mini。循环变压器，26.4B 参数，在约 20GB 内存上运行，并且具有令人惊讶的强大编码基准。 SWE-bench Pro Hard 上的 77.9% 令人印象深刻
author: @vinhnx
summary_en: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B parameter model utilizing a Looped Transformer architecture that operates efficiently within approximately 20GB of VRAM. The model achieves a notable 77.9% score on the SWE-bench Pro Hard benchmark, indicating strong code generation capabilities relative to its compact size.
summary_zh: Thinking Machines推出26.4B参数的Looped Transformer模型，在代码基准测试中表现出色。
full_text_zh: Thinking Machines 的 Inkling 2 Mini。循环变压器，26.4B 参数，在约 20GB 内存上运行，并且具有令人惊讶的强大编码基准。对于这种尺寸的模型来说，SWE-bench Pro Hard 上的 77.9% 令人印象深刻。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: Thinking Machines发布了Inkling 2 Mini模型，该模型采用Looped Transformer架构，参数规模为26.4B，可在约20GB显存环境下高效运行。在SWE-bench Pro Hard评测中，该模型表现出强劲的编程能力，基准得分达到77.9%，展示了紧凑架构在代码生成任务中的显著优势。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4B parameter model utilizing a Looped Transformer architecture that operates efficiently within approximately 20GB of VRAM.
